section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing, when should you move back into the right lane?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you are one vehicle length ahead.,c:After a fixed three-second wait.,d:When the driver waves you back.
note: Return to your lane only after you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror and are sure you have enough room.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, you must:
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Expect oncoming traffic and pedestrians to yield to you.,c:Never yield to anyone.,d:Only yield to vehicles, not pedestrians.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic traveling straight and to pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle, you should signal when?
options: a:After you begin to pass.,b:Just before changing lanes so others see your intent.,c:Only if a police officer is present.,d:Only after you complete the pass.
note: Signal early enough before passing so other drivers understand your intentions in advance.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Identifying dangerous driving situations and taking action to avoid accidents.,b:Defending yourself against poor drivers by getting ahead of them in traffic.,c:Following the vehicle ahead of you at a close distance.
note: Defensive driving means recognizing hazards and taking proactive steps to avoid accidents.

question: Should drivers avoid driving beside large vehicles for long periods?
options: a:True—drivers should be cautious and avoid lingering beside large vehicles.,b:False—it's fine to travel side-by-side with large vehicles.,c:Only true on highways,d:Only true at night
note: Large vehicles have extensive blind spots; avoid driving beside them for extended periods and either drop back or move ahead.

question: When preparing to exit an interstate, when is it appropriate to reduce your speed?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,c:Before reaching the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until you reach the deceleration lane; then reduce speed to the posted advisory speed for the ramp.

question: When the weather is poor, what should drivers do to following distance?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Increase their speed to reach destination more quickly.
note: In bad weather, increase following distance to allow for longer stopping times.

question: What practice best ensures safety when backing your vehicle?
options: a:Honk the horn before reversing.,b:Walk behind the vehicle and check the area before getting in to back up.,c:Rely only on your rearview mirrors.,d:Back quickly to save time.
note: Before backing, walk to the rear of the vehicle to check for children or objects; backing requires extra caution.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow indicate?
options: a:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,b:The protected left turn is about to end.,c:Both of the above.
note: A yellow left-turn arrow warns that the protected turn is ending and drivers must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.

question: If you are very angry after an argument, what is the safest choice?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.,b:Play loud music to distract yourself.,c:Drive on the interstate to vent frustration.
note: Strong emotions reduce driving ability; pause to cool off before getting behind the wheel.

question: Which statement about large trucks is correct?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.,c:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.
note: Large trucks require much longer stopping distances than passenger vehicles because of their size and weight.

question: Why must you use extra caution near a pedestrian carrying a white cane?
options: a:They may be blind or have limited vision and may not see traffic.,b:They are likely to move quickly out of the way.,c:They are signaling you to proceed.,d:They are traffic officers.
note: Pedestrians with white canes or guide dogs are blind or visually impaired; yield the right-of-way and be prepared to stop.

question: Should motorists maintain a safe distance when driving near cyclists?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must give cyclists sufficient operating space and be especially careful when passing or turning near them.

question: When a pedestrian carrying a white cane or using a guide dog is crossing, what must drivers do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,b:Wave them across the street.,c:Proceed because pedestrians must yield.,d:Shout to tell them where to cross.
note: Drivers must always yield to blind or partially blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs along with alcohol?
options: a:It decreases the risk of causing a crash.,b:It has no additional effect.,c:It increases the risk of a crash by intensifying impairment.,d:It counters alcohol impairment.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs (prescription, OTC, or illegal) increases impairment and crash risk.

question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver, you should:
options: a:Relax, focus on driving, and avoid taking other drivers' actions personally.,b:Drive above the posted speed limit to get ahead.,c:Tailgate the vehicle in front to encourage faster driving.,d:Constantly honk to express frustration.
note: Concentrate on driving, be realistic about travel time, obey speed limits, and be forgiving of other drivers to prevent aggression.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?
options: a:They decrease as speed increases.,b:They remain unchanged by speed.,c:They increase as vehicle speed increases.,d:They only depend on vehicle size.
note: Higher speeds result in longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

question: Which light indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution at an intersection?
options: a:A flashing yellow light,b:A flashing red light,c:A solid yellow light
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; drivers should be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, you should:
options: a:Work harder to steer, reduce speed, and drive to a safe area to stop.,b:Turn off your ignition immediately.,c:Honk and stop abruptly in the travel lane.
note: Power steering loss requires stronger steering effort; slow down and pull off the road safely to stop.

question: When being tailgated, what should you do?
options: a:Create extra space in front of your vehicle and avoid sudden braking.,b:Increase speed to put distance between you and the tailgater.,c:Brake suddenly to teach the tailgater a lesson.
note: If someone is following too closely, increase the space ahead of you by changing lanes or slowing gradually to avoid sudden stops.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?
options: a:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.,b:They create vibrations and sound to warn inattentive drivers that they are leaving the travel lane.,c:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
note: Rumble strips produce sound and vibration to alert drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you continually pass other cars on a two-lane road by driving faster than surrounding traffic, you will:
options: a:Get to your destination much faster and more safely.,b:Increase your chances of a collision.,c:Help prevent traffic congestion.,d:Reduce your risk of a ticket.
note: Continuously passing on two-lane roads raises your collision risk each time you pass.

question: What should you remember when sharing the road with large trucks?
options: a:Trucks require longer stopping distances than smaller vehicles.,b:They can stop faster than cars.,c:They have a smaller turning radius.,d:They have better visibility of nearby cars.
note: Because of their size and weight, trucks need more distance to stop and have larger blind spots; be patient and give them space.

question: If your accelerator sticks and the vehicle keeps accelerating, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your four-way flashers.,b:Blow your horn.,c:Slam on your brakes.
note: If the accelerator sticks, turn off the ignition carefully (avoid locking the steering), apply brakes, and move off the road to a safe location. Use four-way flashers to warn others.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, a driver must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.,b:Always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians, even if the pedestrian is wrong.,c:Make sure the pedestrian expects the vehicle before proceeding.,d:Honk to warn pedestrians to clear the road.
note: You must do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian and yield right-of-way to pedestrians, even if they are crossing improperly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive more slowly than the flow of traffic, what will most likely happen?
options: a:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,b:Improve traffic flow.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving significantly slower than normal traffic can impede others and may lead to citations; match the flow unless unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If someone drives much slower than the speed limit and blocks traffic, what should they do?
options: a:Always has the right-of-way.,b:Is a very safe driver.,c:Pull off the road and let following vehicles pass.
note: If driving so slowly that traffic backs up on a two-lane, two-way road, you must pull off and let others pass when safe.

question: Which is not a factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.,d:Perception time.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a primary factor in the calculation.

question: When children are playing in an area you are driving through, you should expect them to:
options: a:Possibly run into the street without looking.,b:Stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Know when it is safe to cross.
note: Children may act unpredictably and run into the roadway; reduce speed and be prepared to stop.

question: What type of sign warns drivers about hazardous conditions ahead?
options: a:Warning signs (usually yellow with black markings).,b:Regulatory signs (white with black markings).,c:Information signs (green or blue).,d:Guide signs (brown).
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potentially hazardous conditions ahead; obey them to reduce accident risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting a highway, when should you start to slow down?
options: a:Once you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road, just before the exit lane.,c:Once you see a toll booth.
note: Get into the exit lane in advance but do not begin to slow down until after you have entered the exit lane.

question: Approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what is required of you?
options: a:Move over a lane if possible, or slow to a safe speed below the posted limit if you cannot.,b:Maintain your speed and pass closely.,c:Stop in your lane directly next to the emergency vehicle.,d:Turn around and find another route.
note: When approaching a stopped emergency or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes away if possible; otherwise slow down and proceed with care.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, which way should you steer?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel into the direction of the skid.,b:Turn your steering wheel into traffic.,c:Overcorrect.
note: If your vehicle skids, stay calm and steer in the direction of the skid until you regain control.

question: Why is night driving uniquely challenging?
options: a:Speed limits are higher at night.,b:Fewer cars on the road make it riskier.,c:Distance and speed are harder to judge in the dark.,d:Traffic signals are less visible for pedestrians only.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes it difficult to judge distance and speed; you can see only as far as your headlights allow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A double solid yellow centerline means:
options: a:No traffic from either direction may pass.,b:Only the lane with a broken line may pass.,c:Passing is allowed for traffic in both directions.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate passing is prohibited for vehicles in both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should never attempt to pass another vehicle in which of these situations?
options: a:On a hill or curve.,b:When approaching an intersection.,c:Both of the above.
note: Do not pass where your view is blocked by hills or curves, at intersections, on railroad crossings, or wherever signs or pavement markings prohibit passing.

question: If your car becomes disabled on the highway, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Stop in the right lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway.,c:Stop where you are.
note: If your vehicle becomes disabled, and it's safe to do so, park with all four wheels off the main-traveled portion of the road.

question: If you hear a siren but cannot immediately see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the curb and stop so you can determine if it is on your street.,b:Keep driving until you spot it.,c:Slow down but keep moving.,d:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: If you hear a siren and don't know where the vehicle is, safely pull to the right and stop until you can confirm it is not headed toward you.

question: Because county highways often have slow-moving traffic, how should you behave?
options: a:Be ready to adjust your speed to the flow of traffic within legal limits.,b:Stay in the left lane and drive above the limit.,c:Pass slow-moving vehicles in curves.,d:Ignore slower traffic and maintain your speed.
note: Anticipate slow vehicles on rural roads and adjust speed or change lanes safely to accommodate them.

question: On a green arrow signal, what must you do before turning?
options: a:Yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection, then proceed.,b:Wait four seconds before going.,c:Turn immediately without yielding.,d:Sound your horn and turn.
note: A green arrow indicates you may turn in the arrow's direction but only after yielding to any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians that remain in the intersection.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:Only if you see a train.,b:If directed by a flagger, or if a stop sign, flashing lights, or lowered gates are present.,c:Never stop unless the tracks are occupied.,d:Only when a train whistle sounds.
note: Stop when directed by a flagger or stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating; also if a train is visible or close enough to be hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow signal, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Maintain your normal speed.,c:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light warns you of potential hazards — reduce speed, be alert, and proceed with caution.

question: To cross a railroad safely, what steps should you take?
options: a:Listen and look both ways, and proceed only when safe.,b:Cross quickly if a train is approaching.,c:Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
note: Always look and listen for trains from both directions and obey signals; never cross until you are sure it is safe.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which of these actions should you NOT take?
options: a:Apply your brakes.,b:Let go of the steering wheel.,c:Press your head firmly against the head restraint.
note: If hit from the rear, keep a firm grip on the wheel, press your body into the seatback and your head against the head restraint to reduce whiplash; do not let go of the wheel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline, what is permitted?
options: a:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,b:You must stay within your lane.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes when safe.

question: Tailgating (following too closely) can:
options: a:Frustrate other drivers and increase crash risk.,b:Reduce collisions by preventing others from cutting in.,c:Be safely used in heavy traffic.
note: Tailgating increases the chance of rear-end collisions and can provoke aggressive reactions from other drivers; keep a safe following distance.

question: A pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog is most likely to be:
options: a:A blind person.,b:A person involved in a traffic study.,c:A person who is hard of hearing.
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

question: When approaching an accident scene you should:
options: a:Stop and gather details even if not involved.,b:Keep moving and focus on driving unless you are involved or help is needed.,c:Drive closer to get a better view.,d:Exit your vehicle to help without assessing the situation.
note: Do not stop at an accident unless involved or emergency help has not yet arrived. Keep attention on driving and watch for people near the road.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Leave the front wheels straight.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if the brakes fail.

question: When making a turn, you must typically do what to your speed?
options: a:Increase it to complete the turn quickly.,b:Maintain your speed.,c:Reduce speed to maintain control and stay in your lane.,d:Come to a full stop every time.
note: Reduce to a speed that allows control of the vehicle, staying within your lane and reacting to unexpected situations.

question: Large trucks are different from passenger cars in that they:
options: a:Have large blind spots.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:Do not need more room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks have large blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop than passenger vehicles.

question: Does talking or texting on a cell phone while driving significantly affect crash risk?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Using a phone while driving is a distraction that increases your risk of being involved in a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Mirrors eliminate blind spots.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked by the rearview mirror alone.,d:Blind spots are only on the right side.
note: Even with mirrors, blind spots remain; large trucks have much larger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Red,d:Blue
note: Solid and broken white lines separate lanes traveling in the same direction; yellow lines separate opposing traffic.

question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are.,b:Safely pull over to the right and stop to allow it to pass.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.,d:Ignore it unless it's a police vehicle.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches, create a clear path by pulling to the right and stopping until it passes; if in heavy traffic, move slowly until you can get out of its way.

question: How should you treat railroad crossings?
options: a:As safe to cross because trains are unlikely.,b:As dangerous and always prepare to stop if necessary.,c:As a safe place to park your vehicle.
note: Railroad crossings can be hazardous; always look and listen for trains and obey signals, signs, and flaggers before crossing.

question: What can happen if you take prescription medication and drink alcohol?
options: a:There will be no effect.,b:It may make you more alert.,c:It can impair your ability to drive safely.,d:It will cancel out the alcohol's effects.
note: Legal prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair driving, especially when combined with alcohol.

question: When rain begins while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,c:Continue at the posted maximum speed.
note: Reduce speed when rain reduces visibility or traction; turn on headlights; if visibility becomes very poor, pull safely off the road and wait.

question: Should you always drive more slowly than the flow of traffic?
options: a:No — driving too slowly can block traffic.,b:Yes — it is always safer.,c:Yes — it is a good defensive technique.
note: While you may need to drive slower in bad conditions, unduly slow driving that blocks normal traffic flow is unsafe and may be illegal.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Shift to neutral and apply steady pressure to the brakes, then pull off the road when safe.,b:Try to pull the pedal up by reaching down.,c:Shift into park immediately.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep eyes on the road, shift to neutral, brake steadily, then stop off the roadway and turn off the engine.

question: If other drivers nearby are displaying anger, what should you do?
options: a:Distance yourself from the situation.,b:Make eye contact and reason with them.,c:Respond with hand gestures to calm them down.
note: Avoid eye contact or gestures that might provoke, and take steps (slow down, change lanes, increase distance) to remove yourself from danger.

question: At a railroad crossing, which statement is true?
options: a:You must stop when directed by a flagger, stop sign, or warning signal.,b:You always have the right-of-way.,c:You can pass other vehicles while crossing tracks.,d:Railroad crossings are private and need not be obeyed.
note: Obey flaggers, stop signs, and warning signals at railroad crossings; always check for trains before crossing and never pass other vehicles on the tracks.

question: How can you lower the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Use tires with proper air pressure.,b:Replace tires with bad tread.,c:Do not speed when the roads are wet.
note: Reducing speed on wet roads and ensuring proper tire pressure and good tread depth reduce hydroplaning risk.

question: What driving habit may help conserve gasoline?
options: a:Slowing down gradually and avoiding unnecessary stops.,b:Accelerating quickly from stops.,c:Sitting with the engine running in drive.,d:Frequent short trips with warm-up idling.
note: Looking ahead to avoid hard braking and accelerating gradually improves fuel economy and reduces wear.

question: Which foot should you use for braking and accelerating?
options: a:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.,b:Use your left foot for braking.,c:Alternate feet for better control.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake to avoid accidental simultaneous inputs and ensure smooth control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Go to the next exit.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.
note: If you miss an exit, continue to the next exit; never stop, back up, or cross the median on the highway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs show?
options: a:The maximum (or minimum) legal speed under ideal conditions.,b:Suggested safe speeds for all conditions.,c:Speeds drivers should follow in heavy traffic.
note: A posted speed limit indicates the maximum (and sometimes minimum) legal speed for ideal driving conditions; slow down when conditions require.

question: If another driver cuts you off in traffic, the best response is to:
options: a:Pull alongside and yell at them.,b:Let it go and continue driving safely.,c:Flash your high beams aggressively.,d:Follow closely to teach them a lesson.
note: To avoid road rage, do not take it personally; let it go and continue driving safely.

question: A railroad crossbuck sign should be treated like which traffic control?
options: a:A yield sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A warning sign with no right-of-way implications.
note: A railroad crossbuck functions like a yield sign; drivers must yield to trains and railroad equipment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking on any hill, what should you do with the parking brake and gear?
options: a:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in 'park'.,b:One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.,c:Your front wheels should be parallel to the road, if there is no curb.
note: Always leave the vehicle in gear or 'park' and set the parking brake when parked on a hill; position wheels to prevent rolling if brakes fail.

question: At a traffic signal showing a steady green arrow, what are drivers allowed to do?
options: a:May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,c:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
note: A green arrow permits turning in the arrow's direction after yielding to any traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: If a traffic control signal is not operating, a driver should:
options: a:Proceed if the intersection looks clear.,b:Treat the intersection as an all-way stop and come to a full stop.,c:Drive quickly through to avoid delays.,d:Yield only to vehicles on the right.
note: When signals are not working, treat the intersection as an all-way stop: come to a full stop, then look and yield before entering.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night, what should you do with your headlights?
options: a:Keep them on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beams.,c:Use your high beams until within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
note: Use low beams when following another vehicle to avoid glaring into the driver's mirrors and obscuring their vision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, you must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Only to vehicles already in the intersection.,c:No one in particular.
note: Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians when making a left turn; complete the turn when it is safe.

question: Do ramps and bridges freeze before adjacent roadways?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Ramps and bridges are exposed to air on both sides and tend to freeze sooner than roads; use extra caution crossing them in cold weather.

question: Why should you use headlights in rain, snow, or fog?
options: a:So others can see your vehicle.,b:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,c:To keep your engine warm.
note: When visibility is reduced by rain, snow, or fog, turning on headlights makes your vehicle easier for others to see. If you use windshield wipers, you must also use low-beam headlights.

question: If heavy smoke covers the roadway ahead, you should:
options: a:Slow, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,b:Turn on high beams and continue.,c:Turn on four-way flashers and keep driving.
note: If smoke reduces visibility, pull off the road to the right and stop in a safe place before proceeding.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams and blinding you, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road.,b:Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.,c:Use your bright lights until the other vehicle dims theirs.
note: When faced with blinding headlights, glance toward the right edge of the roadway until the vehicle passes to avoid being temporarily blinded.

question: Do pedestrians in crosswalks and intersections always have the right-of-way?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections, marked or unmarked, in most situations.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem on a vehicle indicates:
options: a:The vehicle has priority on the road.,b:A slow-moving vehicle.,c:Shoulder work ahead.,d:An all-terrain vehicle.
note: An orange and red triangle marks slow-moving vehicles such as farm equipment or maintenance vehicles.

question: If stopped for a violation or equipment check, which document must the driver present?
options: a:Proof of registration.,b:Your driver license.,c:Proof of insurance.
note: When stopped you should be able to provide your driver license; you are also expected to have vehicle registration and proof of insurance available in the vehicle.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down until it passes you.,c:Continue driving with your flashers on.
note: Upon hearing an emergency vehicle siren, pull safely to the curb or side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: When a pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting at the corner and you plan to turn right, what must you do?
options: a:Wait until the person completes crossing before turning.,b:Tell the pedestrian when to cross.,c:Turn off your engine until they cross.
note: Pedestrians with guide dogs or canes have the right-of-way; wait for them to cross before turning.

question: Leaving a space cushion around your vehicle is important because:
options: a:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.,b:It prevents other drivers from distracting you.,c:It speeds up traffic flow.
note: Keeping a buffer zone provides time and space to respond to mistakes by other road users.

question: A flashing red traffic light requires you to:
options: a:Treat the intersection as if you're traveling the wrong way.,b:Stop and treat the intersection as controlled by a stop sign.,c:Wait until it turns green before proceeding.,d:Slow down but you may not have to stop.
note: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield, and proceed only when safe.

question: If parked in an unusual area, what should you do to minimize hazard?
options: a:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,b:Park five feet from the curb.,c:Leave your reverse lights on.
note: When parking in atypical locations, ensure your vehicle is visible so it does not become a hazard to other drivers.

question: Are drivers always required to stop for a stopped school bus on a two-lane road?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: On a two-lane road, drivers must always stop for a stopped school bus regardless of their direction of travel.

question: True or False: You are required to signal every time you pull away from a curb.
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must use the proper turn signal whenever pulling away from a curb, changing lanes, or turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is accurate?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.,c:Speeding can never be fatal.
note: Both excessive speed and driving much slower than surrounding traffic can be dangerous; speed increases the chance of fatal crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a freeway you should:
options: a:Signal, yield to existing traffic, and enter at the same speed that traffic is moving.,b:Drive slowly so you can check traffic.,c:Signal and expect freeway traffic to yield to you.
note: When merging, accelerate on the ramp to match freeway traffic speed, signal, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes you should not:
options: a:Check your side and rearview mirrors.,b:Signal your intentions.,c:Check for other drivers who may be moving into that lane.,d:Assume the lane is clear without checking your blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and verify no other drivers are moving into the same lane.

question: True or False: Alcohol is the single greatest common factor in fatal motor vehicle crashes.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Alcohol-related crashes are a leading cause of traffic fatalities; alcohol impairs vision and slows reaction time, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign you stop and then you should:
options: a:Look left, then right, then left again.,b:Check your rearview mirror for cars tailgating.,c:Move immediately when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
note: After stopping, scan left, right, then left again before proceeding, as vehicles from the left may be closer or arrive sooner.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It can lower your ability to concentrate on driving.,b:It decreases your chance of having an accident.,c:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.,d:It improves reaction time.
note: Emotional stress reduces concentration and impairs driving ability. It's safer to delay driving when emotionally unstable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you not do?
options: a:Back up on the road or shoulder.,b:Proceed to the next exit and return to the correct exit.,c:Continue on the freeway and find another route.
note: If you miss an exit, never back up on the freeway or shoulder; continue to the next exit or alternate route.

question: Blue traffic signs normally provide information about:
options: a:Construction and maintenance.,b:Motorist services such as rest areas, food, or hospitals.,c:Speed limits.,d:Regulatory restrictions.
note: Blue signs are service signs that inform drivers about motorist services and facilities like rest areas and hospitals.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Collisions are more likely to happen when:
options: a:All vehicles travel at about the same speed.,b:One lane of traffic is faster than the others.,c:One vehicle travels significantly faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,d:All vehicles follow the speed limit exactly.
note: Collisions occur more often when a vehicle's speed differs significantly from surrounding traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for cars entering the freeway?
options: a:Slow down or change lanes when safe to allow them to merge.,b:Maintain your speed and position to avoid disturbance.,c:Speed up to pass them quickly.
note: If possible, merge into another lane or slow slightly to create a gap to allow entering vehicles to merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Rely solely on your mirrors.,c:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
note: Signal in advance, check mirrors, and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to ensure the lane is clear.

question: When entering the interstate, after matching traffic speed and signaling, you should:
options: a:Expect drivers to make room because you have the right-of-way.,b:Merge carefully into an open gap in traffic.,c:Wait for the lane to be completely clear before merging.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait.
note: Identify a gap, accelerate to the speed of traffic, signal, and merge into the gap when it is safe. Do not expect others to yield for you.

question: Drivers must obey instructions from whom at construction sites?
options: a:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.,b:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,c:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.
note: Follow directions from flaggers and posted signs in work zones to ensure the safety of workers and motorists.

question: Which lights should you use to improve visibility reduced by rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in rain or fog; they make your vehicle easier for others to see without causing glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn from a two-way street, where should you begin your turn?
options: a:Near the centerline.,b:Near the right-hand side of the road.,c:On the left of the centerline.
note: When turning left from a two-way street, begin in the lane closest to the centerline and turn into the first legal lane.

question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:
options: a:Maintain a constant speed.,b:Brake hard.,c:Speed up.
note: When being passed, do not speed up or brake suddenly — hold your speed and let the other vehicle pass safely.

question: Which roadway surface is most likely to freeze first in cold weather?
options: a:Bridge,b:Tunnel,c:Intersection
note: Bridges and overpasses can become icy before the rest of the road because they are exposed on all sides and cool faster.

question: If you are taking an over-the-counter medication, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the drug label for warnings about driving.,b:Consume alcohol instead of the medication.,c:Drive regardless of any warning labels.
note: Many non-prescription medications can affect alertness and coordination; read labels and consult a doctor or pharmacist if unsure.

question: What do regulatory signs generally indicate?
options: a:What drivers must or must not do.,b:The presence of nearby hazards.,c:Directions to services.,d:Scenic routes.
note: Regulatory signs (often white rectangles with black lettering) inform drivers of traffic laws and regulations such as speed limits and turn restrictions.

question: Where should a driver direct their attention while driving?
options: a:Stare directly in front of the vehicle.,b:Only focus on the middle of the road.,c:Watch to the sides, ahead, and behind the vehicle.
note: Good drivers scan the road ahead, to the sides, and check behind to be aware of potential hazards.

question: When driving in sleet or snow, you should do which of the following?
options: a:Allow additional distance to the vehicle ahead.,b:Keep windshield and mirrors clear.,c:Both of the above.
note: In wintry conditions keep your windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance because stopping distances are longer on slippery roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When crossing a sidewalk to enter traffic from an alley or driveway, drivers should:
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,b:Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
note: You must stop before entering the sidewalk area from a driveway or alley and yield to pedestrians and traffic.

question: If your car begins to skid, you should steer:
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:To keep the front wheels straight.,c:Opposite the skid immediately.
note: If you skid, steer toward the direction you want to go; as the car straightens, correct the wheel position.

question: When is using your horn appropriate?
options: a:To warn a child about to run into the street.,b:As you travel through intersections.,c:When passing a bicyclist.,d:To express anger at another driver.
note: Use your horn as a warning in situations where someone may not see you and a collision is possible, such as a child stepping into the road.

question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?
options: a:Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.,b:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,c:Inconvenience drivers.
note: Work zone devices warn and direct drivers to keep traffic out of hazardous areas and protect workers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers making a left turn must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.,b:Passing cars.,c:No one in particular.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians before completing the turn.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, where should you look to see what is coming?
options: a:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,b:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.,c:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.
note: Whenever people may cross or traffic lines meet, look to the left and right sides of your vehicle to ensure nothing is coming.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The maximum posted speed limit should be driven only:
options: a:Under ideal conditions.,b:During the day.,c:During the night.
note: Posted speed limits represent the maximum safe speed under ideal conditions; reduce speed for bad weather, heavy traffic, or poor road conditions.

question: When should you be most careful when turning or stopping in rainy weather?
options: a:One half hour after the rain stops.,b:After it has been raining all day.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: Road surfaces are especially slippery during the first half hour of rain because oil and residue on the pavement mix with the rain.

question: You should not use your horn when driving near:
options: a:Blind pedestrians.,b:Other cars in heavy traffic.,c:When visibility ahead is limited.
note: Avoid sounding your horn near blind pedestrians; it may startle or confuse them and create danger.

question: Lines that divide traffic moving in opposite directions are:
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:White lines.,c:Black lines.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

question: When driving in fog you should use:
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Your parking lights only.,d:Hazard lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow because high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Right, toward the side of the road,b:Straight ahead,c:Left, toward the center of the road
note: When parking downhill on a road without a curb, turn the wheels toward the edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: If one of your tires blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Try to steer straight and gradually slow by easing off the gas; avoid hard braking until under control.,b:Brake hard immediately.,c:Maintain speed and steer straight.
note: On a blowout, keep control, slow gradually, and pull off the road when safe; do not brake hard immediately.

question: If a traffic signal displays a green arrow while a red light is also shown, are you allowed to turn in that arrow's direction?
options: a:True,b:False
note: A green arrow means you may proceed in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection, regardless of other red lights.

question: True or False: Because driving involves risk, you should continually improve your driving and observation skills.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Continued improvement of driving skills and observation helps reduce risk and makes you a safer driver.

question: When nearing a railroad crossing, which actions should you take?
options: a:Maintain normal speed and ignore warnings.,b:Slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop.,c:Try to drive around a lowered gate.,d:Speed up to clear the tracks quickly.
note: When you see signs for a railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If gates are down or lights flashing, stop 15–50 feet before the tracks.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Keep your tires properly maintained.,b:Watch out for standing water or puddles.,c:Slow down when roads are wet or slushy.
note: To reduce hydroplaning risk, slow down when roads are wet and avoid standing water; proper tire maintenance also helps.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams in rain, snow, sleet, or fog; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility in these conditions.

question: Do emergency vehicles have the right-of-way when using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:Yes — you must yield to them.,b:No — you have the right-of-way.,c:Only if they are close by.,d:Only if sirens are on and lights are off.
note: Yield immediately to emergency vehicles using sirens and/or flashing lights and follow any instructions they give; be aware they may be traveling in groups.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving in the left lane and others wish to pass, you should:
options: a:Stay in your lane regardless of speed differences.,b:Drive onto the left shoulder to allow faster drivers to pass.,c:Move into the right lane when it is safe to do so.,d:Speed up to prevent being passed.
note: Use the left lane for passing or turning left; move to the right lane when it is safe to allow faster traffic to pass.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They’re difficult to see in traffic.,b:They obey different traffic laws than larger motor vehicles.,c:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Smaller road users are harder to spot and may behave unpredictably; watch carefully to avoid collisions.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, you should:
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the driver can see you.,b:Keep a steady pace within the blind spot.,c:Stay in the blind spot until the driver signals.
note: Do not linger in another vehicle's blind spot; adjust speed to be visible to that driver.

question: Distracted driving is:
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Extremely risky behavior that endangers everyone.,c:Nothing to worry about.,d:An issue only for new drivers.
note: Distracted driving is extremely risky and endangers drivers, passengers, pedestrians, and bicyclists.

question: When driving in fog, what should you do with your lights?
options: a:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.,c:Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.
note: In fog you should slow down and use low beam headlights; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the road and wait for conditions to improve.

question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces you should:
options: a:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,b:Speed up to reduce time spent in the slippery area.,c:Shift to higher gear before descending a hill.
note: Reduce speed before curves or intersections in slippery conditions to avoid losing traction and control.

question: Before changing lanes or passing, what should you do?
options: a:Check mirrors and blind spots, and signal.,b:Only signal if other vehicles are present.,c:Sound your horn to warn others.,d:Flash your headlights and then change lanes.
note: Always check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to scan blind spots, and signal your intentions before moving laterally.

question: At night, which is hardest to see?
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Road signs.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are more difficult to see at night compared to signs and other roadside objects; use caution and proper lighting.

question: A steady yellow light at an intersection warns drivers to:
options: a:Proceed without slowing.,b:Yield to other vehicles.,c:Slow down and prepare to stop because red will soon follow.,d:Speed up to beat the red.
note: A steady yellow warns that a red light is imminent; slow and prepare to stop unless you are already in the intersection and cannot stop safely.

question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what adjustment must you make?
options: a:Visibility is better than on pavement.,b:Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement, so you must slow down.,c:Your tires grip the road better than when you are driving on pavement.
note: On loose surfaces like gravel or dirt, traction is reduced so slow down and be prepared for longer stopping distances and easier skids.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, how should you drive?
options: a:Slow enough to stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,b:Use your high beams at all times.,c:Drive at normal daytime speeds.,d:Stare directly at oncoming headlights.
note: At night reduce speed so you can stop within the distance your headlights illuminate; use high beams only where appropriate and legal.

question: True or False: Orange road signs are used to warn drivers about construction work zones.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Most signs in work areas are orange and diamond-shaped (or rectangular) and often reflective to increase visibility at night.

question: Before changing lanes you should:
options: a:Check your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to ensure the lane is clear.,b:Only check your inside rearview mirror.,c:Slow down dramatically before moving over.
note: Always check mirrors and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.

question: A blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.02% has what effect on crash risk?
options: a:Will double your chances of having an accident.,b:Won't have any effect on your driving.,c:Won't put other drivers at risk.
note: Even low BAC levels can significantly increase the risk of a crash; each small increase in BAC raises risk.

question: If there is no marked crosswalk and a pedestrian begins crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Carefully drive around the pedestrian.,b:Make sure the pedestrian can see you then proceed.,c:Stop and allow the pedestrian to finish crossing.,d:Speed up to pass before they reach your lane.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk.

question: What single action most reduces your risk of serious injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Limiting driving to weekdays.,b:Wearing your seat belt.,c:Staying in the right lane on multilane highways.
note: Wearing a properly fastened seat belt is the most effective way to reduce risk of death or serious injury in a collision.

question: Which is true about sudden weather changes and driving?
options: a:You should adjust your driving when weather changes.,b:You should never change speed for rain or fog.,c:Ignore vehicles behind you in bad weather.
note: If weather changes suddenly, adapt your driving: slow down in rain or fog and be aware of following traffic that may be traveling too fast for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle when:
options: a:There is no solid yellow line preventing you and it is safe and legal to do so.,b:In a curve or on a hill if you judge it safe.,c:By using the shoulder of the highway.
note: You may pass only where permitted by pavement markings and when it is safe and legal; never pass on shoulder or over solid yellow lines.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While waiting in the intersection to complete a left turn, how should your wheels be positioned?
options: a:Signal and keep your wheels straight.,b:Signal and keep your wheels turned to the left.,c:Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
note: Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead while waiting to turn left so a rear-end collision won't push you into oncoming traffic.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Alertness.,b:Coordination.,c:Both of the above.
note: Alcohol and drugs can impair many skills necessary for safe driving, including alertness, coordination, reaction time, and concentration.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Pedestrians who are already in the intersection.,b:Oncoming traffic.,c:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.
note: When turning left you must yield to oncoming vehicles. You must also yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and drivers already in the intersection.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take time to calm down and focus on driving.,b:Drive normally; emotions do not affect driving.,c:Drive faster to get your mind off it.
note: Strong emotions distract attention and can impair driving performance; take time to recover emotionally before you drive.

question: If you are angry from an incident at work, what is the safest action before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to cool off before starting your drive.,b:Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Play loud music to distract yourself.
note: Allow time to calm down before driving; strong emotions distract attention and impair decision-making on the road.

question: Which reminders are important when driving on wet pavement?
options: a:That pavement is especially slippery right after it starts to rain.,b:To give yourself additional space when coming to a stop.,c:That wet roads can cause hydroplaning.
note: Wet roads are especially slick just after rainfall; slow down and increase following distance to reduce the risk of hydroplaning.

question: Is it legal to pass a stopped school bus when its red lights are flashing?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if no children are present,d:Only on multi-lane divided highways
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights are off; exceptions apply on opposite sides of divided roadways.

question: Approaching a parked police, tow, or utility vehicle with flashing lights, what should you do?
options: a:Stop abruptly.,b:Change lanes away and slow to a safe speed if possible.,c:Maintain speed and lane.,d:Park and wait.
note: If possible, move over a lane and reduce speed when passing a stopped vehicle displaying flashing lights; if you cannot change lanes, slow to a safe speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A pedestrian who starts crossing after the 'Don't Walk' signal is flashing is in the middle of the street when your light turns green. You should:
options: a:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Wait until the pedestrian finishes crossing before proceeding.,d:Honk and proceed quickly.
note: Even at a green light, you must yield to any pedestrian still in the intersection; wait until they have finished crossing.

question: You have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?
options: a:Stop and yield to the pedestrians to let them cross safely.,b:Honk to make them hurry up.,c:Speed up and pass in front of them.
note: Even with a green signal, yield to pedestrians in the intersection or crossing against the signal to avoid collisions.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive through, around, or under a railroad gate or barrier?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Never drive through, around, or under railroad gates or barriers — it is illegal and extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, what must you do before changing lanes or passing?
options: a:Always use cruise control.,b:Signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes.,c:Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.
note: On interstates, signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before changing lanes or passing; stop on the shoulder only in emergencies.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim their headlights, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road.,b:Look toward the center of the roadway.,c:Look straight ahead.
note: If the other driver doesn't dim their lights, look toward the right edge of the roadway to avoid direct glare while maintaining lane position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must stop at an intersection when you see which signal?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A steady yellow light.,c:A yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign; you must stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

question: If your vehicle has airbags, what is true regarding seat belt use?
options: a:Seat belts should still be worn for best protection.,b:Seat belts are not necessary.,c:You should wear the belt behind your back.,d:Airbags act as a replacement for child restraints.
note: Airbags enhance safety but are designed to work with lap and shoulder belts; always wear seat belts for maximum protection.

question: A broken yellow centerline between lanes means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction when it is safe.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:There is a construction zone ahead.
note: A broken yellow line allows passing when no oncoming traffic is present and it is safe to pass.

question: At an intersection controlled by a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Slow and yield the right-of-way to traffic already in the roadway or intersection.,b:Always come to a complete stop before proceeding.,c:Ignore vehicles on your left and proceed quickly.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection or roadway you are entering.

question: When driving in fog, which lighting is best to use?
options: a:High beams.,b:Low beams.,c:Four-way flashers.
note: Use low beams in fog because high beams can reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving speed is correct?
options: a:As speed increases, the chance of a fatality in a crash increases.,b:As speed increases, you should increase your following distance.,c:Both of the above.
note: Higher speeds raise the likelihood of fatal injuries in a crash and increase stopping distance, so you must allow greater following distance when driving faster.

question: Anything that requires you to do what could cause a crash?
options: a:Take your attention away from the task of driving.,b:Take your eyes off the road.,c:Take your hands off the wheel.
note: Distractions that remove attention from driving, take eyes off the roadway, or remove hands from the wheel significantly increase crash risk.

question: If confronted by an aggressive driver, you should:
options: a:Move out of their way and avoid confrontation.,b:Challenge them to deter aggression.,c:Speed up to escape.
note: Avoid escalating aggression by yielding space and not engaging with aggressive drivers.

question: A stopped school bus ahead on your side has its red lights flashing. What must you do?
options: a:Stop until the lights stop flashing.,b:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.
note: When a school bus activates its red lights and stop arm, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights are off and students are clear.

question: Blind spots are:
options: a:Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are areas alongside and just behind your vehicle that cannot be seen using mirrors alone; check over your shoulder before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What determines the amount of space you need to cross traffic?
options: a:Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.,b:The presence of a stop sign.,c:The use of your turn signals.
note: Space required to cross depends on road and weather conditions and the amount of oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before turning left, what must you do regarding oncoming traffic?
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound your horn to warn oncoming drivers.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane then turn.,d:Narrow your turn to cross less roadway.
note: When making a left turn yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians; complete the turn only when safe.

question: What is the primary purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:They are mostly decorative.,b:They are only used in construction zones.,c:They provide information and guidance to drivers.,d:They indicate parking spaces only.
note: Highway markings inform drivers about lane positions, passing zones, and upcoming conditions to help safe driving.

question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is allowed from the side next to the broken line and prohibited from the side next to the solid line.,b:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid line.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.
note: When a broken yellow is beside a solid yellow, drivers on the broken-line side may pass when safe; the solid-line side may not.

question: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across lanes at:
options: a:Intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,b:In curves and on hills.,c:Next to churches and schools.
note: Stop lines mark the point where drivers must stop their vehicle at intersections and crosswalks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Pass as slowly as possible to be safe.,b:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle being passed.,c:Pass as quickly and safely as possible, then return to lane.,d:Pass on the right regardless of conditions.
note: Pass quickly and safely, returning to your lane only when you can clearly see the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the effect of excessive speed?
options: a:Saves time so you reach your destination faster.,b:Helps you maneuver around obstacles more easily.,c:Increases the likelihood of severe injury or death in a crash.,d:Has no effect on crash severity.
note: Excessive speed is a common contributing factor to crashes and increases the likelihood of severe injury or death.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Expect the unexpected.,b:Beep your horn.,c:Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.
note: Children can be unpredictable on bikes; slow down, be prepared to stop, and give them plenty of space.

question: If someone is tailgating you on a two-lane road, you should:
options: a:Slow down gradually to encourage them to pass when safe.,b:Speed up to increase distance between you and them.,c:Brake hard to make them back off.
note: If you cannot change lanes, gently reduce speed to let the tailgater pass when it is safe.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crash risks?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Simply say No thanks - I'm driving when offered a drink.,c:Call a taxi only if you feel impaired.
note: The safest choice is to decide in advance not to drive if you plan to drink; relying on willpower after drinking is unreliable.

question: What do downward-facing triangular signs generally tell drivers to do?
options: a:Indicate school zones.,b:Tell drivers to yield.,c:Indicate construction zones.
note: A downward-pointing triangle sign typically means 'Yield' — wait until the road is clear before proceeding.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,b:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: Pentagonal signs warn you of school zones and crossings; be alert for children who may enter the roadway unexpectedly.

question: When you approach a railroad crossing and the crossing signals are flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and look for a train.,b:Slow down and look for a train.,c:Look for a train, then speed up.
note: If warning signals or gates indicate an approaching train, stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail and do not proceed until it is safe.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:Driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.,b:Exiting an expressway.,c:Following a motorcycle.
note: Increase following distance when behind a large vehicle blocking vision, in bad weather, heavy traffic, when exiting expressways, or behind motorcycles/bicycles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On or near any curve or hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a straight roadway with clear view for 500 feet.
note: U-turns must not be made on or near curves or hills where oncoming traffic cannot be seen; they are allowed on straight roadways if not otherwise prohibited.

question: When going somewhere unfamiliar, what should you do before leaving?
options: a:Should depend on road signs to find your way.,b:Only have to know generally where your destination is.,c:Plan your trip in advance.
note: When traveling to an unfamiliar area, plan your route in advance and check a map before you start.

question: Like alcohol or drugs, what effect can drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:Impair your judgment.,b:Make you a better driver.,c:Make you feel better on the road.
note: Sleepiness slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment much like alcohol or other drugs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto a one-way street you should start from:
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb.,b:The lane in the center of the road.,c:Any lane as long as it is safe.
note: When turning left from a one-way onto a one-way street, begin the turn from the far left lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What sequence should you follow to change lanes safely?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot, then change lanes.,b:Signal and immediately change lanes.,c:Check mirrors only and then change lanes.,d:Sound your horn then change lanes.
note: Signal your intent, check rearview and side mirrors, look over your shoulder to verify blind spots, then move when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side at an intersection is blocked, what should you do?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Maintain your speed and look both ways.,c:Slow down and look both ways.
note: When visibility is obscured, stop and creep forward slowly until you can safely see cross traffic before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is trying to pass you, what should you do to facilitate a safe pass?
options: a:Signal to the other driver when it is safe for them to pass.,b:Pull off the road.,c:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust your speed to allow safe passing.
note: Keep right and adjust speed to allow the passing vehicle to safely re-enter the lane.

question: A leaking exhaust system can:
options: a:Make you drowsy while driving.,b:Cause excessive oil use.,c:Require your vehicle to have a tune-up sooner than normal.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow toxic fumes to enter the vehicle and cause drowsiness or even death; have it repaired immediately.

question: For quick, safe turns your hands should be placed:
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:Next to each other on the top of the wheel.,c:On the top and bottom of the wheel.
note: Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel to maintain control during turns and emergency maneuvers.

question: Is it lawful for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full use of a traffic lane; motor vehicles should never attempt to share that lane with a motorcycle.

question: Which action helps prevent crashes by communicating with other road users?
options: a:Drive only on side streets and back roads.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Communicate with other road users (signals, horn when appropriate).
note: Crashes often occur when a driver does something others do not expect; signal intentions, use lights or horn when appropriate to communicate.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, you should:
options: a:Brake hard and steer off the road immediately.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Grasp the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and exit the traffic lane.,d:Turn off the engine and keep steering normally.
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly, gradually slow by easing off the accelerator, lightly apply brakes when safe, and then exit the traffic lane.

question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It lets other road users know your intentions.,b:Because it is illegal to stop signaling before completing the turn.,c:Because turning off a signal is always unsafe.,d:To warn pedestrians only.
note: Signal early and continuously when turning, changing lanes, slowing, or stopping so others can anticipate your actions.

question: Which best describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Looks out for the actions of other drivers.,b:Drives slowly at all times.,c:Travels at a constant speed.
note: A defensive driver anticipates other drivers' actions, stays alert, and avoids relying solely on others to drive safely.

question: If a stopped school bus has its red lights flashing on a public road, you:
options: a:Must stop regardless of whether you are on a private or public road.,b:Need not stop if you are on a private road.,c:Should proceed slowly past the bus.
note: When a school bus activates its red lights and stop arm, traffic in both directions must stop until lights are off and children are clear, regardless of road type.

question: A school bus using flashing amber lights is:
options: a:Changing gears.,b:Warning other motorists the bus will soon stop to load or unload children.,c:Preparing to make a turn.,d:Indicating it is leaving the bus stop.
note: Flashing amber lights warn motorists that the bus will soon stop; drive no faster than 20 mph and be prepared to stop.

question: When changing lanes, the best approach is to:
options: a:Change lanes quickly and often to be efficient.,b:Change lanes while a vehicle occupies your blind spot.,c:Gradually and carefully change lanes when safe.,d:Always accelerate to merge into the next lane.
note: Always change lanes gradually and carefully. Each lane change increases the chance of a crash; only change when necessary.

question: If weather or light conditions require headlights, you should use:
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:High beams at all times.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Hazard lights only.
note: Use low beam headlights in foggy, snowy, or rainy conditions; high beams can reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: A posted advisory speed or speed restriction sign for a curve should be treated how in poor conditions?
options: a:May be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.,b:Is blue with black lettering.,c:Followed more cautiously in poor weather.
note: Advisory speeds for curves are recommendations and should be reduced further in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.

question: If a vehicle is passing you in a no-passing zone, you should:
options: a:Slow down and allow the passing vehicle to return to the lane when safe.,b:Pull off the road.,c:Maintain speed and position so they pass quickly.
note: If someone passes you in a no-passing zone, reduce speed and allow them to merge back safely when possible.

question: If you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing signals or gates, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,b:Prepare to yield to any train at the crossing.,c:Cross the tracks immediately and as quickly as possible.
note: If there are no lights or gates, be prepared to yield to trains and never start to cross unless there is room on the other side.

question: Temporary construction and maintenance signs typically have what colors?
options: a:Red background with green writing.,b:Orange background with black writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.,d:White background with red writing.
note: Work zone signs use orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols to indicate road work and hazards.

question: How should a seat belt be fastened for proper protection?
options: a:Snug across your hip bones and lower abdomen for the lap belt.,b:Loose over your shoulder for comfort.,c:Hidden under the seat for children.,d:Around the waist only, no shoulder strap needed.
note: Lap belts should be snug across the hip bones and shoulder belts should lie comfortably across the chest, with a fist's width of space at most.

question: A dashed white line on a highway means:
options: a:You may cross it to pass or change lanes when safe.,b:You cannot cross to pass.,c:Only left-lane changes are allowed.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: If you suffer a tire blowout while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,b:Tap or pump the brakes.,c:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
note: If a tire blows out, ease off the accelerator, slow gradually, and apply brakes lightly only after the vehicle has slowed considerably.

question: What should your first response be to reduced visibility while driving?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers only.,c:Turn on interior lights.,d:Increase your following distance only.
note: The first action when visibility decreases is to slow down; then use headlights and wipers as appropriate and increase following distance.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive at the posted speed limit.,c:Speed up to clear the danger quickly.
note: Wet, snowy, or icy roads reduce tire traction; slow down and drive cautiously to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited:
options: a:Within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.,b:Only when the vehicle ahead has a slow-moving emblem.,c:When using the right lane to pass a left-turning vehicle.
note: You may not pass within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing; only pass where safe and legal.

question: Yellow pavement lines separate:
options: a:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:Carpool lanes from regular lanes.
note: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads to separate opposing traffic; broken yellow means passing is allowed when safe.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels away from the curb (left).,b:Turn the wheels toward the curb (right).,c:Keep the wheels straight.,d:Turn wheels toward traffic.
note: On an uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb so if brakes fail the vehicle will roll away from traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:
options: a:Yield to pedestrians.,b:Maintain your normal driving speed.,c:Stop and look for nearby police cars.
note: You may turn on a green light unless prohibited by a sign, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

question: When approaching a person using a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Honk and proceed slowly.,b:Stop and wait until the person is well clear of your path.,c:Carefully drive around them while maintaining speed.,d:Wave to get their attention.
note: Yield to blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog; stop until they are well away from your path of travel.

question: Guide signs that show directions and distances are what color?
options: a:Green,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: Guide signs have a green background and provide directional and mileage information to drivers.

question: How do you properly check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Look only at the left side mirror.,c:Rely only on the rearview mirror.
note: A quick over-the-shoulder check is needed to view areas not visible in mirrors before changing lanes.

question: If you stop at a railroad crossing with more than one track, when may you proceed?
options: a:Only after you have a clear view down all tracks and are sure no trains are coming.,b:Immediately after the first train passes.,c:When a flagger waves you across.,d:When other drivers start to go.
note: Wait until you can see down every track and confirm no other trains are approaching before crossing multiple-track railroad crossings.

question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians:
options: a:Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.,b:Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway and exercise extra caution, even if pedestrians are not obeying signals.

question: Which is the most effective restraint system in a crash?
options: a:An airbag by itself.,b:A lap belt only.,c:A lap and shoulder belt used with an airbag.,d:No restraint if the vehicle has airbags.
note: Use both lap/shoulder belts and airbags together for maximum protection in a front-end crash.

question: When do roads typically become very slippery related to rain?
options: a:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.,b:When it has been raining for an hour or more.,c:The day after it rains.
note: Pavement is often most slippery in the first 10–15 minutes of rain because oil and residues on the road surface are brought up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If drivers are passing you on both sides while you are in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the right lane when safe.,b:Maintain your center lane position no matter what.,c:Speed up to prevent being passed.,d:Move to the left lane immediately.
note: On multi-lane highways, keep right unless passing or preparing to turn left; move right if traffic flow requires.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest rule to follow before entering a crosswalk?
options: a:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching in a way that could create danger.,b:Always assume drivers will stop for you.,c:Insist on the right-of-way even in heavy traffic.,d:Enter at any time because vehicles must stop.
note: Though pedestrians often have right-of-way, do not step into traffic when an approaching vehicle cannot stop in time; use caution.

question: When preparing to change lanes, which action should you take?
