options: a:Signal your intentions well before the lane change.,b:Enter the lane immediately without signaling.,c:Count on other drivers to make room for you.
note: Always signal an appropriate amount of time before changing lanes and confirm the maneuver is safe; signaling gives others time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When meeting a steady yellow traffic signal, if you have not entered the intersection you should:
options: a:Stop safely before entering the intersection.,b:Speed up to beat the red.,c:Proceed without change.
note: A steady yellow warns the light will soon turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed cautiously.

question: If the gates at a railroad crossing are down and red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and wait until the gates are raised and the lights stop flashing.,b:Drive around the gates after stopping if no train is in sight.,c:Drive slowly beside the train to clear the crossing.
note: Never drive around lowered gates or through flashing signals. Wait until gates are fully raised and lights stop before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway you should:
options: a:Signal your lane change, check mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check blind spots.,b:Only use the inside rearview mirror.,c:Change lanes without signaling since it's faster.,d:Rely solely on your side mirror.
note: Signal early, check rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to verify your blind spot before changing lanes.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop, whether there’s a stop sign or not.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when you see children.
note: At a school crossing sign, be alert for children and be prepared to stop; always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: What is the proper top-to-bottom order of traffic lights on a vertical signal?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Green, red, yellow.,c:Red, green, yellow.
note: On vertical traffic signals, red is always on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what must you ensure before you begin?
options: a:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,b:Pass only on the right.,c:Watch for oncoming traffic.
note: Before passing, make sure the passing lane is clear and signal your lane change to pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In traffic moving at 50–55 mph, you are least likely to crash if you:
options: a:Drive a few mph faster than most cars.,b:Stay within that speed range and flow of traffic.,c:Drive much slower than surrounding traffic.,d:Constantly change speed to match nearest vehicle.
note: Adjust speed to travel smoothly with surrounding traffic within posted limits; similar speeds reduce multi-vehicle crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection but oncoming traffic is heavy, you should:
options: a:Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.,b:Use the next intersection to turn.,c:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
note: If the light is green, you may enter the intersection and wait for a safe gap before completing your left turn.

question: Hydroplaning can begin at about what speed on a wet road?
options: a:As low as 35 miles per hour.,b:40 miles per hour.,c:45 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can occur at relatively moderate speeds; many tires begin to lose contact with the road as speeds exceed about 35 mph on standing water.

question: Which driving abilities are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Alertness and concentration.,b:Reaction time and coordination.,c:All of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs impair the nervous system, reducing alertness, slowing reaction times, and harming coordination.

question: Reducing the risk of hydroplaning is best accomplished by:
options: a:Slowing down when roads are wet.,b:Increasing your speed.,c:Keeping the same speed as on dry roads.
note: Lowering speed in wet conditions reduces the chance your tires will ride on a film of water (hydroplane).

question: When driving in general traffic it is safest to:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted speed limit.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic to get ahead.,c:Fluctuate your speed frequently to stay alert.
note: Driving at the same approximate speed as traffic, within limits, reduces crash risk caused by speed differentials.

question: What does a “No standing” sign mean at a location?
options: a:You may stop temporarily only to pick up or discharge passengers.,b:You may never stop your vehicle there for any reason.,c:You may park there if the driver remains in the vehicle.
note: A No Standing sign allows temporary stops for passenger pickup or discharge but prohibits parking or waiting.

question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Whenever yielding helps prevent a collision.,b:Never, because it confuses other drivers.,c:Only at uncontrolled intersections.
note: You should yield your legal right-of-way whenever doing so reduces risk of a crash.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do immediately?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn and be prepared to stop.,b:Flash your headlights repeatedly.,c:Start to prepare to slow without signaling.,d:Speed around the child.
note: If a child is about to enter the roadway, a sharp horn blast may warn them and help avoid a collision; be ready to stop.

question: If it seems like your tires have lost contact with the road (hydroplaning), what should you do first?
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.,c:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.
note: If you feel loss of contact, ease off the accelerator and stay off the brakes until the tires regain traction.

question: When driving through a construction zone you should:
options: a:Expect the unexpected.,b:Slightly increase your speed.,c:Expect workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones have changed lanes, workers, and equipment; slow down and be prepared for sudden changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red traffic signal means you must:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection or any crosswalk or stop line.,b:Always stop at the far edge of the intersection.,c:Slow down and proceed if clear.
note: A red light requires stopping before the intersection, stop line, or crosswalk and only proceed when safe and lawful.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In areas with speed limits of 45 mph or less, you must signal continuously during the last how many feet before turning?
options: a:100 feet,b:200 feet,c:300 feet
note: When driving at 45 mph or slower, signal at least 100 feet before making a turn.

question: If you think another vehicle is about to hit you, what should you do first to warn them?
options: a:Use your emergency lights,b:Wave your arms,c:Sound your horn
note: Use your horn to warn drivers or pedestrians who may not see you and may be about to cause a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Passing is prohibited in which of the following locations?
options: a:On hills and curves.,b:Only at intersections.,c:Only at railroad crossings.
note: Passing is unsafe and prohibited on hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings where visibility or conditions prevent a safe lane change.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, you should:
options: a:Increase your speed to reach your destination sooner.,b:Turn up the radio volume and keep driving.,c:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.,d:Open the windows and continue driving.
note: If you notice signs of fatigue like drifting or heavy eyelids, find a safe place to stop and rest or take a short nap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road divided by a broken yellow line, what does this tell you about the road?
options: a:You are on a two-way road.,b:You are on a one-way road.,c:The road is under repair.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate opposite directions of traffic on two-way roads and may be crossed to pass when safe.

question: Are traffic signs and pavement markings mandatory to obey?
options: a:Must always be obeyed.,b:Must be followed only when there is other traffic.,c:Are merely suggestions.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings control traffic flow and must be obeyed.

question: True or False: When an emergency vehicle with sirens and lights approaches, you should pull to the right-hand edge and wait for it to pass.
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must immediately move to the right side of the road and stop to allow an emergency vehicle using audible and visual signals to pass.

question: Double solid yellow centerlines on the road indicate passing is:
options: a:Not allowed from either direction.,b:Allowed only from your direction.,c:Allowed from both directions.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic and prohibit passing for both directions.

question: When a green arrow changes to a steady green light, how should you proceed if you still wish to turn?
options: a:You may still make the turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn and must go straight.,c:You retain the right-of-way to turn without yielding.
note: If a green arrow ends and a steady green remains, you may complete the turn but must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic before turning.

question: Alcohol consumption causes which of the following effects?
options: a:Poor coordination.,b:Loss of concentration.,c:Slower judgment.
note: Alcohol impairs vision, coordination, judgment, and concentration; all of these are affected and increase crash risk.

question: On which traffic signal do you have the right-of-way when turning left?
options: a:A steady green arrow pointing left.,b:A steady green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A green arrow gives protected turn movement; oncoming traffic will be stopped or yielding.

question: Roads are most slippery when:
options: a:It has just started to rain.,b:It has been raining heavily for hours.,c:They are clean and dry.
note: Road surfaces are often most slippery shortly after rain begins as oils on the surface mix with water.

question: A driver should:
options: a:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way to avoid collisions.,b:Assume all drivers obey right-of-way rules.,c:Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.
note: Even with right-of-way, be ready to yield if it prevents a crash; never assume others will follow rules.

question: How must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using siren and lights?
options: a:Drive as close to the right edge as possible and stop.,b:Move into the right lane and slow while continuing to drive.,c:Stop wherever you are immediately, even in an intersection.,d:Speed up to get clear of the emergency vehicle.
note: Drive to the right edge of the road and stop, avoiding stopping in an intersection, until the emergency vehicle has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane beside the broken line only.,c:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid line only.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, vehicles beside the broken line may pass when it is safe; vehicles beside the solid line may not.

question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is permitted.,c:Passing is prohibited.,d:Only turning is allowed.
note: A single broken yellow centerline separates opposing traffic and permits passing from either side when it is safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should always use a turn signal when:
options: a:Changing lanes.,b:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,c:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,d:All of the above
note: Use proper turn signals when changing lanes, entering/exiting parking spaces, or pulling into traffic from alleys or parking areas to communicate with other drivers.

question: Cell phones are a serious source of driver distraction.
options: a:True,b:False
note: While on the road, avoid using cell phones, computers, or other distracting devices except to report a crash or an emergency.

question: If you are involved in a serious crash, what initial actions should you take?
options: a:Stop, check for injuries, and call emergency services if needed.,b:Keep driving to the nearest gas station.,c:Leave the scene immediately.,d:Only exchange phone numbers and continue driving.
note: Stop if possible, check for injuries, call 911 if anyone is hurt, and report the crash to law enforcement when required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is required to pass safely on a two-way, two-lane road?
options: a:Be able to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,b:Only that your vehicle can reach passing speed.,c:That you signal and sound your horn.,d:That the vehicle ahead is turning right.
note: You may pass only if you can see clearly ahead, can return to your lane before oncoming traffic, and the pass is legal and safe.

question: Which of the following does NOT happen after drinking alcohol?
options: a:You are less alert.,b:Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.,c:Your judgement of speed and distance improves.
note: Alcohol impairs alertness, reaction time, and judgment of speed and distance; it does not improve those abilities.

question: Which describes a defensive driver's thinking?
options: a:They anticipate what other drivers might do and prepare to react.,b:They assume other drivers will always do the right thing.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.
note: Defensive drivers predict possible errors by others and are prepared to take evasive action to avoid collisions.

question: Is it safe to use cruise control on snowy or icy roads if you reduce speed?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Do not use cruise control on snow or ice; it can cause loss of control if your tires lose traction.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are most commonly what color background?
options: a:White,b:Green,c:Yellow
note: Regulatory signs inform drivers of laws to obey and are commonly white squares or rectangles with dark letters or symbols.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to return to your original lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:As soon as your front bumper clears the vehicle.,c:After two seconds regardless of distance.,d:When you pass the next mile marker.
note: Make sure you can see the entire passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before moving back into the lane to ensure adequate clearance.

question: Only vehicles with special plates or placards for persons with disabilities may park in designated spaces. True or false?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only with a permit,d:Not always required
note: Spaces marked 'Reserved Parking for Persons with Disabilities' may be used only by vehicles displaying Persons with Disabilities plates, Disabled Veteran plates, or disabled parking placards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down without stopping.,c:Merge to the right.
note: A flashing red light means stop completely, yield right-of-way, and go only when safe.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is approaching while you want to pass a pedestrian walking along the road, you should:
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Maintain speed; the oncoming driver must stop for you.,c:Use your horn to make the pedestrian move aside.
note: When faced with multiple hazards, handle them one at a time—let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian if safe.

question: Is it illegal in Iowa to read, write, or send a text while driving?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Iowa law prohibits any driver from reading, writing, or sending text messages while driving unless the vehicle is safely stopped off the traveled portion of the roadway.

question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?
options: a:Use only the interior rearview mirror.,b:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.,c:Rely solely on the side mirror.,d:Use the backup camera while moving forward.
note: Even with properly adjusted mirrors, look over your shoulder to visually check blind spots before changing lanes.

question: Are motorists required to yield to pedestrians even if pedestrians cross against the traffic light?
options: a:False,b:True
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the street and be prepared for pedestrians who may misjudge signals or cross unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the centerline shows a solid line on your side and a broken line on the other, may you pass?
options: a:False,b:True
note: If the solid line is on your side, you may not pass; traffic next to the broken line may pass when it is safe.

question: True or False: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road allow passing from either direction.
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing by vehicles traveling in either direction; you may not cross the centerline to pass.

question: When a school bus displays flashing red lights, when must vehicles stopped behind it remain stopped?
options: a:Until the bus retracts its stop arm and resumes motion.,b:Until all students are off the bus.,c:Until a crossing guard waves them through.,d:Only until the lights stop flashing.
note: Do not pass a school bus with red flashing lights and extended stop arm; remain stopped until the bus withdraws the stop arm and moves.

question: How can you avoid panic stops while driving?
options: a:Watch for hazards well ahead of you.,b:Accelerate heavily through intersections.,c:Drive with your window partly down.
note: By scanning far ahead and anticipating hazards you can adjust speed smoothly and reduce the need for sudden stops.

question: What can happen when alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both may be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both may be reduced.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs can amplify impairing effects, often producing greater impairment than either substance alone.

question: When driving at night, what general precaution should you take?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use high beams regardless of other traffic.,c:Look directly at oncoming headlights.,d:Drive at the posted daytime speed limit.
note: At night increase following distance to allow extra reaction time; use high beams only when they won't blind other drivers.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, the correct action is to:
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow gradually, and use the brakes lightly to pull off the road.,b:Apply the brakes hard and hold them.,c:Immediately pull over quickly without slowing.
note: On a blowout, keep control, ease off the gas, brake gently when stable, and exit the roadway safely.

question: A curb painted red indicates:
options: a:No parking, standing, or stopping.,b:A loading zone.,c:Reserved passenger pick-up/drop-off area.
note: Red curbs indicate no stopping, standing, or parking is permitted.

question: What is true about driving on a wet roadway?
options: a:As you drive faster, your tires become less effective.,b:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,c:Water does not affect cars with good tires.
note: As speed increases on wet roads, tires become less effective at removing water and hydroplaning risk increases.

question: How should you check your vehicle's blind spots?
options: a:The inside rearview mirror.,b:The outside rearview mirror.,c:Over your shoulders.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; to check them, look over your shoulder before changing lanes or merging.

question: Why shouldn't you follow other cars too closely?
options: a:You may miss seeing the road between the cars.,b:You might not have enough time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.,c:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.,d:It improves fuel economy.
note: Following too closely reduces your stopping time if the vehicle in front slows or stops suddenly, increasing collision risk.

question: Which behavior may help you identify an aggressive driver?
options: a:Erratic or improper lane changes.,b:A large number of passengers in the vehicle.,c:A tendency to drive slowly.
note: Aggressive drivers often make unsafe or erratic lane changes, tailgate, or exhibit other risky behaviors; give them space.

question: Which of these can impair your driving ability?
options: a:All of the above,b:Marijuana,c:Cold remedies
note: Many substances, including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over-the-counter remedies, can impair driving ability.

question: What is the best response when someone is following you too closely (tailgating)?
options: a:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.,b:Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.,c:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.
note: If another vehicle follows too closely, slow down and let it pass when safe — avoid sudden braking or speeding.

question: Slowing down only to look at a crash or other unusual event (rubbernecking) primarily does what?
options: a:Causes traffic congestion.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Improves traffic flow.
note: Avoid slowing down to look at collisions or other unusual events because it reduces traffic flow and may cause additional congestion and crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate from a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for and identify a gap in traffic, then accelerate to merge.,b:Immediately enter the far-right lane and speed up quickly.,c:Use the shoulder to accelerate to traffic speed.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and then enter at will.
note: On short ramps without acceleration lanes, identify a safe gap before entering and avoid stopping in the travel lane while waiting.

question: If you start to feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Stop driving.,b:Open your window.,c:Get some coffee.
note: Drowsy driving is dangerous and similar to impaired driving. If you feel tired, stop driving and rest before continuing.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Inattentive driving.,b:Following other vehicles too closely.,c:Excessive speed for conditions.,d:All of the above.
note: Inattention, tailgating, and speeding for conditions are common causes of crashes; safe driving requires attention and appropriate speed and spacing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should generally:
options: a:Accelerate to a speed that matches freeway traffic.,b:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
note: Use the on-ramp to reach freeway speed so you can merge smoothly; yield to traffic already on the roadway.

question: If the driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk, what must you do?
options: a:Stop, proceeding only when all the pedestrians have crossed.,b:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,c:Change lanes, look carefully, and pass the stopped vehicle.
note: Do not pass a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk; there may be pedestrians you cannot see. Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in a line waiting at a stop sign and there is no cross traffic after vehicles ahead have cleared, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop again at the stop sign or line before proceeding.,b:Proceed through without stopping a second time.,c:Slowly roll through the stop sign.,d:Honk to move traffic.
note: You must bring your vehicle to a full stop at the stop sign or stop line each time and yield to approaching traffic before proceeding.

question: Consuming which substances can impair driving and may result in DUII arrest?
options: a:Beer, wine and liquor.,b:Controlled substances and some prescription medicines.,c:All of the above (including inhalants).
note: A wide range of intoxicants—alcoholic beverages, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription or over-the-counter medications—can impair driving.

question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slam on the brakes immediately.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and gradually slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving at the same speed until you reach a service station.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the wheel firmly, stay in your lane, ease off the accelerator, and slow gradually before braking lightly and pulling safely off the road.

question: As you near the top of a hill, you should:
options: a:Be prepared to stop if necessary.,b:Speed up slightly to clear the hill.,c:Maintain speed without change.
note: Because you cannot see what is over the crest, be ready to stop for hazards that might be just out of sight.

question: After stopping for a train that has passed, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Wait for signal lights to stop flashing and look for a second train.,b:Look for a second train only.,c:Wait only for the gates to raise.
note: After a train passes, be alert for a second approaching train and do not go until all warning signals are off and gates are up.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They are more difficult to see than cars.,b:Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.,c:They rarely use their headlights.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots; it can also be hard to judge their speed and distance.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a minimum BAC of:
options: a:0.05 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: In Iowa (and federally), drivers 21 and older are considered legally impaired at a BAC of 0.08% or higher.

question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Drive through if no crossing traffic is present.,b:Come to a complete stop and wait for a green (right turn may be allowed if not prohibited).,c:Continue because they have the right-of-way.,d:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A steady red requires a complete stop. Right turns on red are permitted unless a sign prohibits them and you must yield to traffic and pedestrians.

question: A single broken white line between lanes on a multi-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers may change lanes when safe.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers may not pass.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to change lanes.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and indicate lane changes are permitted when safe.

question: Drowsy drivers may:
options: a:Drive so poorly that they appear to be intoxicated.,b:Stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.,c:Stay safe by drinking strong coffee.
note: Drowsiness can impair driving similar to alcohol; simple measures like opening a window or caffeine are inadequate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?
options: a:The pedestrian always yields.,b:The driver must yield.,c:Whoever started moving last.,d:The faster party.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without traffic lights, regardless of where the pedestrian is.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway, how should you respond?
options: a:Make room for merging traffic when possible.,b:Assert your right-of-way by speeding up.,c:Hold your lane and refuse to yield.,d:Brake suddenly to prevent merging.
note: When safe, change lanes or adjust speed to help vehicles merge; cooperative driving reduces crash risk.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what is the correct action?
options: a:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.,b:Maintain speed and remain in your lane.,c:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren, pull to the right edge and stop until it has passed.

question: Near heavy trucks, other drivers should allow for:
options: a:Decreased stopping distance for the truck.,b:Increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:Quieter operation of the larger vehicle.,d:Faster acceleration by the truck.
note: Large vehicles require greater stopping distance. Smaller vehicle drivers should keep visible positions and avoid lingering in blind spots.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a flashing yellow traffic signal, drivers should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Turn on their headlights.,c:Increase their speed.
note: A flashing yellow signal warns of a potential hazard; reduce speed and be prepared to react to changing conditions.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is approaching at night, your headlights should be:
options: a:On the low beam setting.,b:On the high beam setting.,c:Off; use parking lights.
note: Do not use high beams when another vehicle approaches; switch to low beams to avoid blinding the other driver.

question: When borrowing an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Begin driving immediately since all vehicles operate the same.,b:Check and familiarize yourself with the vehicle's controls and correct any defects before driving.,c:Hide from your friend that you are unfamiliar with it.
note: Take a few minutes to locate and operate turn signals, headlights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, horn, and correct any defects before driving.

question: How do blind spots compare on larger vehicles versus smaller ones?
options: a:Larger vehicles have larger blind spots.,b:Larger vehicles have smaller blind spots.,c:All vehicles have identical blind spots.,d:Larger vehicles have no blind spots.
note: The bigger the vehicle, the bigger the blind spots, especially to the rear and sides; be cautious when passing or following trucks.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing where you see no train, when must you stop?
options: a:Only if a police officer is present.,b:If a stop sign is posted or flashing red lights/gates are in operation.,c:Only when you hear a train horn.,d:Never stop if you don't see a train.
note: Stop whenever flashing red lights are active, a crossing gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals stop, or a train is visible or close enough to be hazardous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop your vehicle in which situations?
options: a:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.,b:Where there is a red traffic light.,c:Both of the above.
note: You must stop whenever a police officer directs you to, and at steady or flashing red traffic lights as required by law.

question: Many crashes are caused by which driving behavior?
options: a:Driving too fast for conditions.,b:Consistently checking mirrors and blind spots.,c:Yielding the right-of-way.,d:Using turn signals.
note: Excess speed for conditions is a frequent factor in crashes; adapt speed to weather, road, and traffic conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection but opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until you can see all lanes you need to cross before turning.,b:Accelerate quickly when the first lane clears.,c:Proceed if an oncoming driver waves you.,d:Turn partially and then stop.
note: Do not begin a left turn until you can see that all lanes you must cross are clear and it is safe to complete the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are required to stop in which of these situations?
options: a:When approaching a stop sign.,b:When a traffic officer orders you to stop.,c:Where there is a red light.
note: Drivers must stop at stop signs, at illuminated or flashing red lights, or whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop. (All listed situations require stopping.)

question: A distraction while driving is defined as:
options: a:Anything that improves your driving focus.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to drive more cautiously.,d:Only using a cellphone while driving.
note: A distraction is anything that diverts attention from driving and can lead to collisions, injury, and property damage.

question: Before driving you should remove snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:All windows.,b:Just the windshield.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: Clear all windows and mirrors so you have an unobstructed view in all directions before you drive.

question: What does an 'End school zone' regulatory sign indicate?
options: a:The end of a reduced speed school zone.,b:The beginning of a reduced speed zone.,c:The speed limit is 20 mph.
note: An 'End school zone' regulatory sign marks the end of the reduced speed school zone; do not exceed the posted school zone speed during indicated times.

question: Before entering an intersection you should look:
options: a:Left, right, then left again.,b:Only to the left.,c:Only to the right.,d:Straight ahead only.
note: Look to both left and right before entering; look left again because vehicles from the left are closer to you.

question: Which of these is a dangerous habit when driving in a work zone?
options: a:Tailgating other vehicles for short distances.,b:Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment.,c:Both of the above.
note: In work zones, adjust speed to conditions, avoid tailgating, and watch closely for workers and equipment.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing midway across the street, you should:
options: a:Not stop for them.,b:Stop and yield to them.,c:Honk to hurry them along.,d:Speed around them quickly.
note: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing illegally; stop to avoid hitting them.

question: At a railroad crossing you should be alert for which of the following?
options: a:Vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings (e.g., school buses, hazmat trucks).,b:Multiple trains approaching from different directions.,c:Both of the above.
note: Approach railroad crossings with extreme caution, watch for vehicles required to stop at all crossings, and be aware that more than one train may be approaching from either direction.

question: If a pedestrian begins to cross in front of your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop; yield the right-of-way.,b:Flash your lights to warn them.,c:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,d:Sound the horn and continue driving.
note: Always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and be especially cautious where children or others may enter the roadway.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Traffic in the lane next to the broken line may pass, but traffic next to the solid line may not.,b:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,c:Both lanes may pass.
note: When a broken yellow line is next to a solid yellow line, only traffic beside the broken line may cross to pass when it is safe.

question: A red arrow shown on a traffic signal means what?
options: a:A driver must stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.,b:A driver must proceed slowly through the intersection.,c:A driver must stop and then proceed when the way is clear.
note: A red arrow requires drivers to stop and remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign indicates otherwise.

question: On an undivided highway, if an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and lights, what should you do?
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Speed up to clear traffic.,c:Drive slowly until it passes.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles by pulling over to the right edge of the road and stopping when safe to do so.

question: Only what can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC) and alcohol's effects on the body?
options: a:Drinking coffee or caffeine.,b:Eating high-fat foods.,c:Time—the passage of time.,d:Taking a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and remove alcohol; no food, drink, or other methods rapidly reduce BAC.

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady yellow arrow, what should drivers do?
options: a:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,c:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns the protected turn is ending; stop if it is safe to do so unless you are already in the intersection.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of drug?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant that slows reactions and impairs judgment.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similar to:
options: a:The effect that alcohol has.,b:The effect that amphetamines have.,c:The effect that anger has.
note: Fatigue impairs judgment and reaction time comparably to alcohol; extended wakefulness can simulate high BAC effects.

question: Construction zone signs are generally what shape and color?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.,b:Round with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Temporary work zone signs use an orange background with black letters or symbols to warn drivers of construction hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass?
options: a:No, you may not.,b:Yes at any time.,c:Yes if no oncoming traffic is visible.,d:Yes when the shoulder is clear.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing from either direction except when turning into or out of driveways or designated left-turn areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Driving faster or too slow for conditions and exceeding the posted speed limit.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on driving.,d:Following all traffic laws.
note: Driving above the posted speed limit or at speeds inappropriate for conditions commonly contributes to crashes. Drive with the flow of traffic within legal limits.

question: If you need to slow on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Firmly apply your brakes.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: On slippery surfaces, lift off the accelerator to reduce speed first; apply brakes gently if additional slowing is needed.

question: What does a single dashed yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Vehicles in either direction may pass when it is safe.,b:Traffic flows in the same direction on both sides.,c:Passing is prohibited.,d:Turn lanes are ahead.
note: A single dashed yellow line means opposing traffic may pass when it is safe to do so and not prohibited by other signs.

question: If you're in an intersection when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Continue through the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the middle of the intersection.,c:Pull to the left and stop.,d:Block the intersection until it passes.
note: If in an intersection when an emergency vehicle approaches with siren and lights, clear the intersection and then pull to the right and stop to yield.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign, what should you do?
options: a:Slow and yield the right-of-way to traffic or pedestrians in the roadway you are entering.,b:Always come to a full stop before proceeding.,c:Yield only to traffic approaching from the left.
note: A yield sign requires slowing and yielding to traffic or pedestrians; stop only if necessary for safety.

question: An orange-colored road sign usually warns of:
options: a:Construction or maintenance work ahead.,b:The start of a no-passing zone.,c:A school zone ahead.
note: Orange signs with black symbols indicate temporary traffic control for construction, maintenance, or emergencies.

question: A 'Merging lanes' sign means drivers should:
options: a:Speed up to get ahead of merging traffic.,b:Be prepared to change lanes or allow other traffic to merge.,c:Stop and wait for others to merge.,d:Ignore merging vehicles.
note: A merging lanes sign indicates two lanes will become one; drivers should change lanes or allow others to merge safely.

question: When roads are slippery, you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Use alternate routes only.
note: On slippery roads you need extra stopping distance, so increase following distance and drive cautiously.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Drivers who arrived before you.,b:The driver on your right regardless of arrival time.,c:The driver who signals first.
note: At a four-way stop, yield to any vehicle that arrived before you and proceed in turn when it is safe.

question: Is it lawful to drive at night using only your parking lights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: You must use headlights when driving at night; parking lights alone are not sufficient or lawful for driving.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:When changing lanes, turning, or pulling toward/away from a curb.,b:Only when backing up.,c:Only on the highway.,d:Never; mirrors are sufficient.
note: Always glance over the shoulder toward the direction you intend to move to verify no one is in your blind spot before changing position.

question: A diamond-shaped road sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A road hazard or warning.,b:An interstate route.,c:A school crossing sign.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs indicating potential hazards or conditions that may require caution.

question: Where is parking prohibited among these choices?
options: a:On a hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: It is unlawful to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane; when parking on the street, position your vehicle within the required distance from the curb.

question: What do double solid yellow centerline markings mean regarding passing?
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing is allowed only from your direction.,d:Passing is allowed only for trucks.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing across them for traffic in either direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, you should never do which of the following?
options: a:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,b:Attempt to pass or change lanes within an intersection.,c:Check for other drivers trying to enter the same lane.
note: Never attempt to change lanes or pass while inside an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots before moving over.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A red arrow showing to the right means you may:
options: a:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.,b:Turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and not turn in the arrow's direction until a green signal permits it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at an intersection with a flashing red light. How should you respond?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, and proceed when it is safe.,b:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,c:Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then go when the way is clear.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:Pollution.,b:A loss of hearing.,c:Carbon monoxide poisoning.
note: A leaking exhaust can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment; replace defective parts immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what should you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway.,b:Blow your horn to warn approaching vehicles.,c:Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.
note: You must stop or yield as required and give the right-of-way to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway when entering from a driveway or private road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:A speed that is faster than is reasonable and prudent.,b:The maximum speed limit.,c:A speed that is safe for existing conditions.
note: You must drive at speeds that are reasonable and prudent for conditions and always within posted limits.

question: When parallel parking facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.,b:Keep your wheels straight.,c:Turn your wheels away from the side of the road.
note: When parked downhill, turn the front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.

question: If you find a vehicle defect that could affect safety, you should:
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible.,b:Wait until you can afford repairs.,c:Drive more slowly until you can fix it.
note: Any defect that affects safe operation should be repaired promptly before driving when possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a red light is displayed but a green arrow points your direction, when may you proceed?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop.,c:Only after the green arrow turns off.
note: A green arrow indicates a protected movement; if you are in the designated lane and it is safe, you may proceed in the arrow's direction, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.

question: True or False: You need to allow as much following distance when behind a motorcycle as behind a car.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly, but because of their vulnerability and maneuverability, you should allow at least three to four seconds following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: True or False: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest you can drive under any condition.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Posted maximum speeds apply under ideal conditions; you must slow down when conditions (weather, traffic, visibility) require it.

question: In poor weather, what is the correct steering and braking approach?
options: a:Steer and brake smoothly and gradually.,b:Steer off the road immediately.,c:Brake hard to stop quickly.,d:Drive in the lowest gear always.
note: In inclement weather avoid sudden steering or braking; smooth, gradual inputs help maintain traction and control.

question: Smoking and preparing to smoke while driving is:
options: a:A distracting activity that can impair driving.,b:Helpful to maintain alertness.,c:Not affecting driving ability.
note: Smoking while driving can divert hands and eyes from driving and is a distracting activity.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: It is illegal to do which of the following while passing another vehicle?
options: a:Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing.,b:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone.,c:Both of the above.
note: You must not cross the centerline to pass on hills, curves, at street or railroad crossings, where signs prohibit passing, or where a solid yellow line borders your lane. Passing is especially prohibited where you cannot see far enough ahead to complete the pass safely.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Frequently to monitor traffic behind you.,b:Only when slowing down.,c:To check if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
note: Regularly scan mirrors to be aware of traffic; use shoulder checks to verify blind spots.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side.,c:Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.
note: Large trucks have much larger blind spots; mirrors do not eliminate blind spots, so a shoulder check is necessary.

question: A broken yellow centerline beside your lane indicates what?
options: a:You may pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.,b:No passing is permitted.,c:You must stay in your lane regardless.,d:This is a one-way street marking.
note: A broken yellow line on your side means passing to the left is allowed when safe and legal.

question: What do five-sided (pentagonal) road signs typically indicate?
options: a:School zones or school crossings.,b:No passing zones.,c:Speed limits.,d:Railroad crossings.
note: Pentagonal signs warn drivers they are entering a school zone or near a school crossing—be especially alert for children.

question: What does a steady red arrow displayed on a traffic light mean?
options: a:Traffic may not proceed in the direction indicated by the arrow.,b:You may turn after coming to a complete stop.,c:Proceed with caution without stopping.,d:Flash your headlights and go.
note: A steady red arrow prohibits movement in the direction of the arrow until a green signal is shown.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:
options: a:Are always aware of the risks they take.,b:Often lack sufficient mental and physical control to drive safely.,c:Become better drivers because they are more careful.,d:Are unaffected if they feel sober.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, vision, reaction time, and concentration; it is unsafe to drive after drinking.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and can't find the owner, you must:
options: a:Leave a written notice with your name, address, and the accident circumstances.,b:Must stay until the police arrive.,c:Have done as much as you can.
note: If you can't locate the owner, leave a note with your contact information and a description of what happened and report the incident if required.

question: If you experience a sudden tire blowout while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Grip the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually, using the brakes lightly.,b:Brake as hard as possible immediately.,c:Pump the brakes rapidly.,d:Turn off the ignition and coast to a stop.
note: Hold the wheel firmly, keep the vehicle straight, lift off the accelerator, and apply the brakes lightly to slow gradually after a blowout.

question: Should drivers yield the right-of-way to a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog, cane, or other assistive device?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Pedestrians with assistive devices have the same rights as other pedestrians; drivers must yield to them and proceed cautiously.

question: If there are oncoming vehicles on your left and parked vehicles on your right, you should steer:
options: a:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,b:Closer to the oncoming vehicles.,c:Closer to the parked vehicles.
note: Split the difference—steer a safe path between oncoming traffic and parked cars to avoid hazards.

question: Because motorcycles and scooters are small and hard to see, you should:
options: a:Make constant visual checks.,b:Share a lane with a motorcycle.,c:Slow down when driving only occasionally.
note: Motorcycles can hide in blind spots; continuously check mirrors and over your shoulder to spot them.

question: What does a double solid yellow line down the center of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing by vehicles traveling in either direction except for limited lawful turns when safe.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Gradually slow down and pull off the road; do not immediately slam on brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas and immediately apply the brakes hard.,c:Speed up and try to reach the nearest exit quickly.
note: On a tire blowout, ease off the accelerator, hold the steering wheel steady, avoid hard braking, and gradually slow down to a safe area off the road.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle, you should:
options: a:Slow down and continue driving.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to go around you.,d:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: Yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right and stopping until the emergency vehicle has passed; if in an intersection, clear it first then stop.

question: When backing up, what is the safest procedure?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window while slowly backing.,b:Rely only on mirrors to see behind you.,c:Open the car door to look behind you.,d:Back quickly to clear the area fast.
note: Before backing, check behind your vehicle; while backing, turn and look over your shoulder through the rear window—don't rely solely on mirrors or sensors.

question: To help others see you as daylight fades, you should turn on:
options: a:Your low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: Turn on low-beam headlights at dusk to increase visibility to other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but pedestrians are in the intersection, you must:
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:Assert your right-of-way and proceed.,c:Wait for pedestrians to step aside.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the intersection, even when the light is green, especially when turning.

question: You should allow extra following distance when you are:
options: a:Following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.,b:Following a small passenger car.,c:Following a station wagon.
note: Give extra space when following large vehicles that have limited rear visibility or that block your view of the road ahead.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of what?
options: a:Being late for an appointment.,b:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,c:Missing an exit.
note: Fatigue increases the risk of poor decisions, slower reactions, and falling asleep at the wheel, which can cause crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A sign that reads “Reduced speed, 35 mph” indicates what?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.,b:The reduced speed begins at the next speed limit sign.,c:You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced zone.
note: Reduced speed signs indicate that the posted lower speed limit begins at the sign and you must slow to the posted speed at that point.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition is it legal to make a left turn on a red light after stopping?
options: a:Only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street and no sign prohibits it.,b:Whenever you have stopped and the intersection is clear.,c:Only when turning from a two-way street onto another two-way street.
note: After a complete stop, turning left on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, unless signs forbid it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which action should you never do when changing lanes?
options: a:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.,b:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,c:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors and blind spots and signal; never make abrupt or spontaneous lane changes.

question: If involved in a minor collision with no injuries and little damage at an intersection, what should you do with your vehicle?
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane, if possible.,c:Not move your vehicle for any reason.
note: If no one is injured and it is safe, move your vehicle out of the travel lane to avoid blocking traffic.

question: When you drive through a construction zone, what behavior should you avoid?
options: a:Stopping to watch the workers.,b:Passing the construction zone carefully and not 'rubbernecking',c:Decreasing your following distance.
note: Do not 'rubberneck' or slow down to watch; pass construction zones carefully and maintain a safe following distance.

question: A double solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is permitted if safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing traffic and indicate passing is not allowed.

question: May you drive around lowered railroad crossing gates under any circumstances?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:When the lights have stopped flashing.,c:When the train has passed.
note: You must stop for crossings when signals indicate an approaching train; never go around lowered gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After a traffic stop by law enforcement, a driver should:
options: a:Remain in the vehicle with hands visible and wait for instructions.,b:Exit the vehicle and approach the officer's car immediately.,c:Unlock the trunk and step out.
note: When stopped by police, stay in your vehicle with hands visible and follow officer instructions for safety.

question: A motorist making a left turn must yield to an oncoming bicyclist. True or false?
options: a:True,b:False,c:Only if in a bike lane,d:Only at night
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming bicycles the same as you would to oncoming motor vehicles.

question: When sharing the road with motorcycles, you must:
options: a:Allow the motorcycle a full lane and not share the lane with them.,b:Drive on the shoulder beside them.,c:Expect them to use only half the lane.
note: Motorcycles have full use of a lane; give them the same lane width and room to maneuver as other vehicles.

question: A steady green light at an intersection means you may:
options: a:Proceed through the intersection if the way is clear, yielding to pedestrians and other traffic as required.,b:Speed up to clear the intersection.,c:Stop and check both ways before moving.
note: A steady green allows you to go through the intersection, turn right or left unless prohibited, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, then proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and drive through carefully.,c:Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
note: A flashing red light means stop; proceed only when the intersection is clear and it is safe to do so.

question: Why should you avoid making sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Large vehicles travel faster than small vehicles.,b:Large vehicles need longer stopping distances due to size and weight.,c:Small vehicle drivers cannot see large vehicles in their rearview mirrors.,d:It improves fuel economy of the truck.
note: Large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop; sudden stops can lead to rear-end collisions because they may not be able to stop in time.

question: A good rule regarding passing is:
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and safe.,b:Always pass on the right.,c:Try to get to the front of slow traffic to see better.
note: Passing increases collision risk; keep pace with traffic and pass only when needed and within the law.

question: What must you do when you approach an octagonal traffic sign?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to others, and proceed when safe.,b:Slow down but not necessarily stop.,c:Turn in the direction indicated by other traffic.
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means stop; yield to traffic and pedestrians with the right-of-way.

question: True or False: Driving at night using only parking lights is unlawful.
options: a:True,b:False
note: At night you must use headlights; parking lights alone are not sufficient or legal for driving in the dark.

question: Broken yellow lines are used to:
options: a:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate where passing is allowed.,b:Indicate no passing zones.,c:Separate lanes moving in the same direction.
note: Broken yellow centerlines separate opposing traffic and mean passing is allowed when safe.

question: When driving in fog, you should use high beam headlights.
options: a:True,b:False
note: Use low beam headlights in fog; high beams reflect off moisture and reduce visibility.

question: Is it lawful to exceed the speed limit when passing another vehicle?
options: a:False,b:True
note: It is illegal to exceed the posted speed limit even when passing another vehicle.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Stop and yield to other traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when clear.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Ignore the signal if no other vehicles are present.
note: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield to others, and proceed only when safe.

question: If you are in an accident and someone is injured, what should you do?
options: a:Not move the injured unnecessarily; keep them warm and give first aid if trained.,b:Move the injured away from the scene immediately.,c:Always leave the injured where they are and wait for others.
note: Do not move injured persons unless absolutely necessary; untrained movement can worsen injuries. Keep them warm and render first aid if you are able until help arrives.

question: Signs requiring mandatory compliance are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do; failing to obey them may lead to penalties.

question: Is driving while impaired by medication ever permitted?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you don't feel drowsy.,c:If it is prescribed by a physician.
note: It is illegal to drive under the influence of any substance that impairs your ability to drive safely, including some prescription and over-the-counter medications.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal means you should:
options: a:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,b:Stop before crossing.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light is a warning to slow down and proceed with caution through the intersection.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you at a safe distance?
options: a:Maintaining a steady speed.,b:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.,c:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.
note: Maintain a steady speed and signal your moves in advance so the driver behind can maintain a safe distance.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that what color will soon appear?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady green.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red, so you should prepare to stop if it is safe to do so.

question: When driving on snowy or icy roads, what should you avoid using?
options: a:Cruise control.,b:Low gears.,c:Slow, gradual inputs.,d:Extra following distance.
note: Do not use cruise control on snow or ice; you need full control to adjust speed and react to slipping.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Continue; you have the right-of-way.,b:Stop and allow the pedestrians to finish crossing.,c:Pull to the right and drive around them.
note: You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a marked crosswalk and wait until they have finished crossing before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these driving practices is correct regarding passing and lane changes?
options: a:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes or passing.,b:When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror before returning.,c:Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes. Also use mirrors and check your blind spot, and ensure you can see the passed vehicle's headlights before returning to your lane.

question: According to Iowa's Implied Consent Law, which is true?
options: a:An arrested driver may be asked to submit to chemical testing and refusal can lead to license withdrawal.,b:Refusing chemical testing has no consequences.,c:Only residents are subject to testing.
note: Under implied consent, a peace officer can request breath, blood, or urine tests if they suspect impairment; refusing or failing can result in immediate license suspension.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The larger vehicle.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.,d:The driver going straight must yield.
note: If two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: When driving on roads that may be slippery, what should you avoid?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,b:Reduce your following distance.,c:Always drive at the maximum speed limit.
note: Avoid using cruise control on slippery roads and reduce speed and following distance to allow for safer handling.

question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:As soon as your front bumper clears the passed vehicle.,c:After three seconds regardless of distance.,d:When the driver you passed waves you in.
note: Only move back when you can clearly see the entire vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, ensuring adequate clearance.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you and creates a hazard, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: If someone cuts in too closely, lift off the accelerator to increase braking distance rather than braking hard or swerving.

question: What is the correct sequence when a school bus prepares to stop to load/unload children?
options: a:Amber lights begin flashing to warn, the bus stops with red lights flashing and the stop arm extends, then children board or exit.,b:Red lights flash first then amber lights.,c:Stop arm extends, then amber lights begin flashing, then bus stops.
note: Amber warns drivers to slow; when red lights flash and stop arm extends, vehicles must stop until children are safely boarded or off the roadway.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The combination can multiply the effects of alcohol or the medication.,b:The medicine cancels out the alcohol.,c:Alcohol helps the medicine work better.,d:Nothing changes.
note: Alcohol mixed with other drugs can increase impairing effects, sometimes dramatically, raising crash risk and side effects.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:When entering a street from a garage or alley.,b:When your traffic signal is a green arrow.,c:When they are on a road to your left and you have reached an unmarked intersection at the same time.
note: You must yield when entering from an alley, driveway, or garage and to pedestrians on intersecting sidewalks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does driving speed affect how far your vehicle travels after you brake?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: The faster you drive, the longer your stopping distance will be. Keep a safe following distance in high-speed traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you, what is the correct action?
options: a:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,b:Decrease your speed.,c:Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
note: If you impede traffic by driving significantly below the flow, pull off the road to let others pass when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Does increasing speed lengthen the time and distance needed to stop for unexpected moves by other drivers?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: The faster you travel, the longer it takes to stop to respond to unexpected actions by other drivers.

question: If you are being tailgated, you should:
options: a:Move over to the right if an open lane exists, or slow gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass.,b:Immediately brake to warn the tailgater.,c:Maintain your speed regardless.
note: If a right lane is available, change lanes; if not, slow gently when safe to let the tailgater pass—do not brake abruptly.

question: True or False: It is safe to stop on railroad tracks if moving with a stream of vehicles for a short time.
options: a:True,b:False
note: It is illegal and unsafe to stop on railroad tracks. Always ensure there is room for your entire vehicle on the far side before crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.,b:Honk to alert approaching vehicles.,c:Drive slowly so approaching traffic will move out of the way.
note: Always come to a complete stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to pedestrians and traffic, and proceed only when safe.

question: Which statement about backing your vehicle is true?
options: a:Backing is always dangerous and requires extra caution.,b:Backing is dangerous only for large vehicles.,c:Backing is safe if you have a helper present.
note: Backing is hazardous because rear visibility is limited; always check behind you and use a helper if available.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may cross a dashed white line when:
options: a:It is safe to change lanes.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:At any time regardless of conditions.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when safe.

question: If you see animals near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Speed up to scare them away.,c:Quickly swerve into the next lane.
note: Animals may bolt or travel in groups; slow down and be prepared to stop safely rather than swerving suddenly.

question: You see pedestrians near the roadway. What should you do?
options: a:Pass at normal speed since pedestrians should stay off the road.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution, prepared to stop.,c:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,d:Speed up to move past the area quickly.
note: Watch for any pedestrian who may cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road where you are driving, slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Turn into first lane.,b:Turn into any lane.,c:Turn into second lane.
note: When turning from a two-way onto a one-way street, turn into the first available legal lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, it is safe to return to your lane when:
options: a:You can see the vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:You have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.,c:You cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
note: Return to your lane only after you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, indicating adequate space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:
options: a:Only during school hours.,b:Only if you see children present.,c:At all times when they are directing traffic.,d:Only on weekdays.
note: Drivers must obey crossing guards' directions when they are controlling traffic near schools.

question: When approaching a stopped school bus with lights flashing and its signal arm extended, you must:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the arm is retracted and the bus moves.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are visible.,c:Pass at normal speed but watch for children.,d:Wait until a police officer directs you to stop.
note: You must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights and extended arm, regardless of travel direction, until it resumes motion.

question: What is a common effect of driving at excessive speed?
options: a:Increases your ability to react to hazards.,b:Often leads to high-risk decision-making.,c:Does not increase the chance of a crash.,d:Reduces braking distance.
note: Driving too fast for conditions commonly contributes to crashes and often leads to risky decisions; it rarely saves meaningful time.

question: Interstate driving requires drivers to do what?
options: a:Have ability to safely drive at increased speeds and be constantly alert.,b:Only drive at the posted minimum speed.,c:Only use cruise control.
note: Safe interstate driving requires alertness and the ability to safely operate at higher speeds and adjust to traffic flow.

question: When passing a vehicle that just parked at the side, you should:
options: a:Assume the driver might open a door and use extra caution.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Slam on your brakes as you pass.
note: Expect doors to open and pedestrians to step out; slow and pass with caution.

question: When is it necessary to use low beams?
options: a:On a lighted street.,b:At all times on a freeway.,c:In foggy or misty conditions.,d:When following another vehicle closely at night only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, rain, or mist because high beams will reflect and cause glare.

question: When passing a large vehicle, a small-vehicle driver should be prepared for:
options: a:Loud noises only.,b:Wind gusts and turbulence from the larger vehicle.,c:Excess pollution that obscures vision.,d:Lights being flashed.
note: Large vehicles can create strong wind gusts that can affect smaller vehicles; be prepared to maintain control during the pass.

question: What can continuous hard braking on ice or snow cause?
options: a:Locking of the front wheels and loss of steering.,b:Faster stopping than gradual braking.,c:Prevention of brake freeze.,d:Increased tire traction.
note: Hard continuous braking on ice or snow can lock the wheels and cause a loss of steering; brake and steer smoothly and gradually.

question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Brake hard just before the curve.,b:Reduce your speed before the curve.,c:Activate your turn signal as you enter the curve.
note: Slow down before you enter a curve when conditions require; excessive speed in a curve can reduce control and increase stopping distance.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a collision.,b:If stopped for a citation or involved in a collision, or upon an officer’s request.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.,d:Never required to show insurance.
note: You must have evidence of financial responsibility with you and show proof of insurance and license to an officer upon request after a stop or collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is beside your lane, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If you are on an expressway.,c:When traffic ahead is clear to pass.
note: If the broken yellow line is next to your lane you may cross it to pass if there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

question: Why should you increase following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To see around the vehicle and to avoid being in its blind spots.,b:Because it creates a drafting effect.,c:Because large vehicles always drive slower.
note: Large vehicles block view and have blind spots; giving extra space improves visibility and safety.

question: Consistently looking far ahead while driving on the highway helps you do what?
options: a:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Spot upcoming police officers for tickets.,c:Keep up with the fastest vehicles only.
note: Scanning far ahead helps you anticipate traffic changes and hazards so you can adjust speed and lane position early and smoothly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from curb parking, you should:
options: a:Wait for a gap large enough to accelerate to the speed of traffic.,b:Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Wait for two vehicles to pass then merge.
note: Merge only when there is a gap sufficient to reach the speed of other traffic safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady green traffic light allows you to:
options: a:Proceed through the intersection at a safe speed if the way is clear.,b:Increase your speed to pass other vehicles.,c:Ignore pedestrians crossing the street.
note: A steady green light permits movement through the intersection, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing a vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, you should:
