options: a:Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,b:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,c:Return to the right side immediately regardless of distance.
note: After passing, move back into your lane only when you can safely see the entire passed vehicle ahead of you in your mirror.

question: If you are near a large commercial vehicle, which practice is recommended?
options: a:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,b:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large commercial vehicles have extensive blind spots; avoid remaining beside them for long periods.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what speed should you always travel?
options: a:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,b:At the speed limit.,c:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.
note: Drive at a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions — never above the legal limit and slow down when conditions are poor.

question: What problems can sudden wind gusts on highways cause?
options: a:They only affect very large vehicles.,b:They only reduce visibility.,c:They can create steering and control problems for all vehicles.,d:They have no effect at highway speeds.
note: Strong winds can cause visibility issues and physically move vehicles; while especially hazardous to large vehicles, all vehicles can be affected.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what is the correct action to regain control?
options: a:Ease off the accelerator and steer into the direction of the skid.,b:Brake hard immediately.,c:Turn off the ignition, then steer.,d:Shift to neutral and hold the wheel straight.
note: When skidding, lift off the gas and steer in the direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding to regain balance and control.

question: You should allow extra following distance when behind which type of vehicle?
options: a:Station wagon,b:Passenger car,c:Motorcycle,d:Truck
note: Allow extra space behind motorcycles because they can stop more quickly and are harder to see at night.

question: At a stop sign with no crosswalk, drivers should stop:
options: a:Before entering the intersection.,b:Only if pedestrians are present.,c:Only if a police officer is watching.,d:At the center of the intersection.
note: Stop at the stop line if present; if not, stop before entering the crosswalk or, if none, before entering the intersection.

question: Reaction time becomes slower after doing what?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.,d:Exercising.
note: Alcohol impairs reflexes, vision, judgment, and reaction time, increasing crash risk even at low levels.

question: You should always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:
options: a:There isn't enough room on the far side for your vehicle to clear the tracks.,b:The crossing is in a city with frequent trains.,c:You are carrying two or more children.
note: Do not stop on the tracks; only enter if there is room on the far side to completely clear the tracks.

question: When backing up your vehicle you should:
options: a:Look through the rear window.,b:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,c:Press hard on the gas pedal.
note: When reversing, turn and look through the rear window while backing up slowly; do not rely solely on mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is NOT a safe interstate driving practice?
options: a:If you miss an exit, continue to the next exit.,b:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,c:Change lanes without signaling.
note: On interstates you must signal before changing lanes; if you miss an exit, proceed to the next one; slower traffic should stay right.

question: In foggy conditions, should you use high beam headlights?
options: a:False,b:True
note: In fog, use low beam headlights or fog lights; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

question: If a vehicle begins to hydroplane (skid on water), you should:
options: a:Quickly apply the brakes to regain traction.,b:Release the accelerator and steer gently—do not immediately brake.,c:Turn the steering wheel sharply to correct the skid.,d:Shift into neutral and rev the engine.
note: If hydroplaning, attempt to regain control by easing off the accelerator and steering smoothly; do not immediately apply brakes.

question: Double solid yellow lane markings indicate:
options: a:Neither lane may pass.,b:The lane to the right may pass.,c:Both lanes may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposing flows of traffic and mean passing is prohibited for drivers in both directions.

question: Which sections of roadway tend to freeze more quickly in cold weather?
options: a:Flat.,b:Curvy.,c:In the sun.
note: In cold or wet weather, certain areas such as shaded or otherwise protected sections may freeze faster than the rest of the road; be cautious in these areas.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, what is the safest way to pass a bicyclist going in the same direction?
options: a:Slow down and wait until no oncoming traffic, then pass leaving sufficient space.,b:Continue driving; the bicyclist must move out of your way.,c:Do not pass until you reach a traffic signal or stop sign.
note: Pass bicyclists as you would other vehicles but give them ample space (at least 3 feet) and only pass when it is safe to do so.

question: An important step when making a turn is to:
options: a:Check traffic in all directions before executing the turn.,b:Always move to the left lane.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Check rear and side traffic as well as pedestrians to ensure it is safe to turn.

question: Parking on the shoulder of a freeway is allowed:
options: a:Only in an emergency, otherwise it is prohibited.,b:If you turn on four-way flashers.,c:To consult a map briefly.
note: Stopping on a freeway shoulder is illegal except for emergencies; flashers do not make regular stops lawful.

question: A red and white triangular sign at an intersection indicates:
options: a:Always come to a full stop.,b:Slow and be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Speed up if an emergency vehicle approaches.,d:Pedestrian crossing ahead.
note: A red and white yield sign requires you to slow and yield to any vehicles or pedestrians, and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, what immediate actions should you take?
options: a:Blow your horn, steer right, and brake.,b:Blow your horn, steer left, and brake.,c:Blow your horn, steer right, and accelerate.
note: Honk to attract attention and try to escape to the right; if a collision is unavoidable, braking reduces impact.

question: You may continue carefully through an intersection with a yellow light if:
options: a:You are already within the intersection when the light turns yellow.,b:There are pedestrians crossing.,c:An emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, proceed through carefully.

question: When driving in work zones, you should:
options: a:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b:Pass the vehicle ahead as soon as possible.,c:Avoid tailgating and maintain a safe following distance.,d:Ignore posted speed limits.
note: Keep a safe distance from barriers, equipment, workers, and vehicles; increase following distance and do not tailgate in work zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if what is true about traffic on the street you are turning onto?
options: a:Traffic on the street moves to the left.,b:You increase your speed before the turn.,c:Traffic on the street moves to the right.
note: You may turn left onto a one-way street only when traffic on that street moves to the left (and no sign prohibits the turn).

question: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) depends on each of the following except:
options: a:The type of alcoholic beverage consumed.,b:Your body weight.,c:How much time passes between drinks.
note: BAC depends on amount drunk, body weight, and time elapsed; the beverage type does not affect BAC directly.

question: Drivers distracted by which device have an increased crash risk?
options: a:Cell phone.,b:CD player.,c:Radio.
note: Using a cell phone is a significant distraction and increases crash risk, though any audio device can also distract.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Brake abruptly to stop the skid.,b:Stay off the brakes and steer to regain control.,c:Pump the brakes rapidly.,d:Turn off the ignition immediately.
note: If your vehicle skids, avoid braking as it may worsen the skid; steer gently to regain control and slowly reduce speed.

question: Which action helps reduce the risk of a rear-end collision?
options: a:Release the gas pedal and let your vehicle slow before applying the brakes.,b:Avoid sudden stops.,c:Before stopping, check your mirrors and blind spots for traffic.
note: To avoid sudden stops, ease off the accelerator to slow and then apply steady brake pressure so drivers behind you have time to react.

question: What effect does consuming alcohol while taking drugs have?
options: a:It reduces the effect of both.,b:It can increase the effects of both alcohol and the drugs.,c:It cures the illness.,d:It has no impact.
note: Combining alcohol with drugs can increase the impairing effects of both, making driving much more dangerous.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right.,b:Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.,c:Turn your wheels to the left.
note: After signaling and checking traffic, stop parallel to the vehicle ahead of the parking space before beginning your parking maneuver.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, you should:
options: a:Drive in the center of the roadway.,b:Attempt to drive through if the water looks shallow.,c:Turn around and find another route—do not drive through floodwater.,d:Speed through to create a wake and clear the water.
note: Never drive on flooded roads; even shallow water can hide hazards or sweep your vehicle away. Turn around and seek another route.

question: Before turning, you should:
options: a:Signal several seconds before the turn.,b:Immediately turn the wheel without signaling.,c:Increase speed then turn.
note: Activate your turn signal three to four seconds before turning to alert other road users.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You, if you are traveling faster.,b:The vehicle on your right.,c:The vehicle that signals first.
note: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: What affects your ability to stop quickly and safely?
options: a:Other cars on the road.,b:The time of day.,c:The condition of the road.
note: Your stopping ability is greatly affected by road conditions; reduce speed on slippery or poor surfaces to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers reach a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on your right has the right-of-way.,c:Either driver may go first.,d:You may proceed without yielding.
note: Yield to the driver on your right when two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop simultaneously; proceed only when it is safe.

question: What is a blind spot?
options: a:An area you cannot see without turning your head.,b:The area directly behind your vehicle.,c:The area you see in your rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas beside or slightly behind your vehicle that you cannot see using mirrors alone and require a head check.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic on the freeway?
options: a:Using your rearview and side mirrors.,b:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,c:Using your rearview mirror.
note: When entering a freeway, use your side mirrors and look over your shoulder to see and anticipate traffic when merging.

question: If your vehicle has a two-piece seat belt, you should:
options: a:Use both the lap and shoulder belts together.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: Always wear both the lap and shoulder portions of a two-part belt for full protection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you ever start across an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red?
options: a:No, you must not enter and block the intersection.,b:Yes, if you entered on a yellow light.,c:Yes, if you entered on a green light.,d:Only if emergency vehicles are present.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it completely before the light changes; blocking intersections is prohibited and may lead to a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct procedure for making a right turn?
options: a:Signal, slow, and approach the corner in the lane nearest the right curb before turning.,b:Signal and move toward the centerline before turning.,c:Signal then speed up to complete the turn quickly.
note: Signal in advance, slow, and make the turn from the lane nearest the right curb, staying close to the curb during the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A traffic signal showing a green arrow plus a steady red light means you may:
options: a:Drive only in the direction of the green arrow.,b:Drive straight ahead only.,c:Wait for a solid green light to proceed in any direction.
note: If a green arrow is displayed, you may proceed only in the direction of the arrow and only when the intersection is clear.

question: When merging onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Use the entrance ramp to match freeway speed and yield to traffic.,b:Merge without checking mirrors to avoid hesitation.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.
note: Accelerate on the ramp to match traffic speed, use mirrors and blind spot checks, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

question: A broken yellow centerline signifies which of the following?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline permits crossing to pass on the left when there is no oncoming traffic. Do not cross a solid yellow to pass.

question: When may you legally drive around or under a railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never.,b:When you can clearly see in both directions.,c:When the warning lights are off.,d:If only one track is present.
note: Do not go around or under any lowered railroad crossing gate. Wait until gates are raised and you can safely proceed.

question: What do two solid yellow lines down the center of the roadway indicate?
options: a:No passing from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed for both directions.,c:You may pass if the road is clear.,d:Only trucks may pass.
note: Two solid yellow lines mean neither direction may cross to pass; they separate opposing traffic and indicate a no-passing zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A light that flashes yellow on and off generally means:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
note: A flashing yellow light is a caution signal — reduce speed and be prepared to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, if you and the driver on your left arrive simultaneously, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your right.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: In very foggy conditions, you should slow down and use which lights?
options: a:High beam headlights,b:Emergency flashers,c:Low beam headlights
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility; fog lights may be used in addition to low beams.

question: If no stop line or crosswalk marking is present where a stop is required, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:In the intersection to get a better view.,d:200 feet from the intersection.
note: Stop at the nearest point before entering the intersecting roadway that gives you a clear view of approaching traffic without entering the intersection.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle on the roadway ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain the posted speed to drive through it.,b:Avoid the puddle if possible.,c:Shift into neutral while driving through the water.
note: To reduce the risk of skidding or hydroplaning, avoid deep puddles when you can and slow down for wet areas.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid out of control, what should you do about braking?
options: a:Apply the brakes lightly.,b:Stay off the brakes.,c:Pump the brakes.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay off the brakes; steer to correct the skid until you regain control.

question: On long trips, how can you help prevent drowsiness?
options: a:Turn up the radio to stay alert.,b:Slow down to conserve energy.,c:Stop regularly for rest and stretching breaks.,d:Drink lots of coffee while driving.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest and stretch to avoid drowsiness on long trips.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady green traffic light, you should:
options: a:Proceed only if no pedestrians or vehicles remain in the intersection.,b:Stop if a police officer is nearby.,c:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop.,d:Immediately accelerate through without scanning.
note: Yield to pedestrians and vehicles still in the intersection; proceed but be ready to stop if the light changes or hazards appear.

question: A single dashed white line separating lanes of traffic means:
options: a:Drivers may pass or change lanes when it is safe to do so.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to pass or change lanes when it is safe.

question: Approximately how far might it take a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph to stop?
options: a:About 400 feet.,b:About 50 feet.,c:About 125 feet.,d:About 200 feet.
note: Large, fully loaded tractor-trailers require much longer stopping distances—up to around 400 feet at 55 mph—so give them extra space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a highway from an entrance ramp, what is the correct general practice?
options: a:Stop at the end of the ramp, then enter slowly.,b:Accelerate to match the speed of traffic and merge when there is a gap.,c:Enter at a speed above traffic to get ahead.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, signal, and merge into a safe gap.

question: Just before you change lanes, what is a key thing you should do?
options: a:Check your rearview mirror only.,b:Quickly turn your head to look for vehicles in your blind spot.,c:Rely solely on your side mirror.
note: Before moving into another lane, check side and rearview mirrors and then glance over your shoulder to verify your blind spot is clear.

question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:You should speed up to beat the light.,b:You do not need to signal to turn from that lane.,c:The green arrow protection is ending; prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning time is ending; you should prepare to stop and yield to oncoming vehicles before turning.

question: A solid white line between lanes on a two-lane road means:
options: a:Lanes move in the same direction and passing or lane changes are discouraged.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is prohibited.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is allowed.
note: Solid white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction; crossing them is discouraged and often prohibited.

question: An arrow painted on the pavement indicates that drivers in that lane:
options: a:Must make the movement indicated by the arrow.,b:May choose to ignore the arrow if traffic is light.,c:Must come to a complete stop before moving.
note: Pavement arrows direct lane movement; drivers in the lane are expected to follow the arrow unless otherwise directed by a signal or sign.

question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing red signal, what must you do?
options: a:Stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.,b:Reduce speed and proceed with caution without stopping.,c:Stop and remain until the light stops flashing.
note: A flashing red signal is treated like a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the blood may affect a driver's what?
options: a:Judgment and physical coordination.,b:Right-of-way privileges.,c:Knowledge of traffic laws only.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can impair judgment, coordination, and reaction time, which are critical for safe driving.

question: When driving in rain you must:
options: a:Use your low beam headlights.,b:Only use high beam headlights.,c:Use parking lights instead.,d:Turn off your headlights.
note: In rainy conditions, use low beam headlights to improve visibility and reduce glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On the freeway, if you see a 'Merging traffic' sign you should:
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by moving over when it is safe.,b:Always remain at your present speed.,c:Honk at incoming traffic.
note: When traffic is merging, adjust speed or change lanes safely to allow vehicles to enter the freeway smoothly.

question: Double solid yellow centerlines mean:
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the left.,c:Passing is permitted from the right.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate opposing traffic and prohibit passing in both directions.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,b:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,c:It has no effect on either.
note: Alcohol diminishes reaction time, coordination, vision, and the ability to judge speed and distance, while also impairing judgment.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:On all sides of the vehicle (front, back, left, and right).,b:Only in front of your vehicle.,c:Only on the left and right sides.,d:Only behind your vehicle.
note: Maintain space on all sides to allow time to react to hazards; do not crowd adjacent lanes.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:Stop and yield the right-of-way.,b:Stop and wait for the green light.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you always do?
options: a:Signal your intentions regardless of visible traffic.,b:Signal only if other vehicles are present.,c:Only signal when driving at night.
note: Always signal before changing lanes or turning, even if you think no other road users are present.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Follow the flagger's directions.,b:Follow what surrounding traffic does, even if it conflicts with the flagger.,c:Assume the flagger is mistaken and ignore them.,d:Speed through the work area to avoid delays.
note: Obey the flagger's directions, reduce speed, and use caution; failure to do so is illegal and dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are in a designated left-turn lane with oncoming traffic. What should you do before turning?
options: a:Keep your front wheels pointed straight ahead until you begin the turn.,b:Turn your front wheels left in anticipation of the turn.,c:Move to the left of the center lane to prepare.
note: Signal well before the turn, keep your wheels straight while waiting to avoid being pushed into oncoming traffic if rear-ended, and turn only when safe.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:
options: a:Pull off the road, turn on emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.,b:Get out and flag down the first passing vehicle.,c:Sound your horn to warn passing cars.
note: If you stop on the shoulder, use emergency flashers, remain in the vehicle if safe, and call for assistance; walking along an interstate is dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates:
options: a:The maximum safe speed under ideal conditions.,b:Only a suggested safe speed.,c:The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
note: Speed limits denote the maximum legal speed for ideal driving conditions; adjust downward for hazards or poor conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates:
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.,b:The suggested safe speed in bad weather.,c:The speed that all drivers must travel at all times.
note: Speed limits are the maximum (or minimum) legal speeds under ideal conditions; slow down for poor conditions as needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a steady yellow light and have not entered the intersection, you should:
options: a:Come to a safe stop.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal is about to turn red — prepare to stop if you can do so safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing yellow signal at an intersection indicates you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be alert; you do not need to stop unless required by other conditions.

question: If an oncoming car has very bright headlights at night, you should:
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Stop until the other driver passes.,c:Look below their headlights.
note: Avoid looking directly at the bright lights; glancing toward the right edge of the road helps keep your vehicle safely on course.

question: Is it legal to drive alongside a motorcycle in the same lane?
options: a:True,b:False
note: You must not share a lane with a motorcyclist; motorcycles require a full lane to maneuver safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, you should aim to be driving at which speed?
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to 10 mph slower than the speed of traffic on the freeway.,c:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.
note: When merging, enter at or near the speed of the traffic already on the freeway so you can merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:If there is an available passing lane and the other vehicle is turning left.,b:Even if it requires driving off the pavement.,c:On a narrow bridge.
note: You may pass on the right when there is a designated lane or when the vehicle ahead is making a left turn and there is room to pass safely without leaving the pavement.

question: If you drink socially, what helps ensure you avoid driving impaired?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.
note: Having a sober ride home prevents driving while impaired; coffee or showers do not reduce blood alcohol.

question: Which factor affects how alcohol is absorbed by the body?
options: a:Weight,b:Height,c:Intelligence
note: Absorption and effects of alcohol vary with weight, biological sex, the presence of food, and the amount consumed.

question: When marked by two solid white lines across a traffic lane, what is true about the crosswalk?
options: a:Motor vehicles have the right-of-way over pedestrians in crosswalks.,b:When pedestrians are in crosswalks, they should be given the right-of-way.,c:No one has the right-of-way in a crosswalk.
note: Crosswalk markings show where pedestrians should cross; you must always stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk.

question: If you see a driver’s left arm extended downward, what are they signaling?
options: a:They intend to turn left.,b:They intend to turn right.,c:They intend to stop or slow down.,d:They are indicating a lane change to the left.
note: A downward extended left arm indicates the driver intends to stop or slow; adjust your driving accordingly.

question: Headlights are required when visibility is less than how many feet?
options: a:500 feet.,b:300 feet.,c:100 feet.
note: Iowa law requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is limited to 500 feet or less.

question: A red flashing traffic light is equivalent to a:
options: a:Solid red light.,b:Stop sign.,c:Yield sign.,d:No entry sign.
note: A flashing red traffic signal has the same meaning as a stop sign; come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.

question: A faulty suspension can cause:
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Minimal effect on ride stability.
note: Suspension problems affect vehicle control and handling; excessive bouncing or poor control indicate repair needed.

question: When ridden on public roads, bicycles are legally considered which of the following?
options: a:Hazards,b:Vehicles,c:Dangerous
note: When bicycles are being used on roadways they are considered vehicles. Bicyclists and motorists must follow the same rules of the road.

question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or pulling away from a curb is:
options: a:Required by law and a good habit.,b:Only necessary if other traffic is present.,c:Not required when driving slowly.,d:Optional during daylight.
note: You must signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes or turning and always before pulling away from a curb to inform other road users.

question: When taking any medicine, what should you do regarding driving?
options: a:Ask a doctor or pharmacist about possible effects on driving ability.,b:Open your window and drive more slowly.,c:Have someone follow you home at all times.
note: Many legal medications can impair driving; consult your doctor or pharmacist about side effects before driving while using them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane must you turn left when leaving a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the right curb.,c:The center lane.,d:The lane marked for through traffic only.
note: When turning left from a one-way street, begin the turn from the lane closest to the left curb (the leftmost lane) and enter the closest available lane.

question: Before backing out of your driveway when children are playing nearby, what should you do?
options: a:Walk to the rear of the vehicle and check that the way is clear.,b:Sound your horn so they will hear you.,c:Rev the engine to warn them.
note: When children are nearby, get out and check behind and around your vehicle before backing to ensure no one is in the path.

question: To prevent hydroplaning you should:
options: a:Ensure tires have good tread depth and proper inflation and reduce speed in rain.,b:Only worry about tire inflation.,c:Drive faster to cut through water.,d:Use your parking lights.
note: Good tire tread, correct inflation, and reduced speed in wet conditions help prevent hydroplaning.

question: It is important to reduce your speed under which conditions?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads.,b:When the road is wet or slippery.,c:All of the above.
note: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections or railroad crossings, in poor weather, and where visibility or traction is reduced.

question: If your vehicle’s right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct recovery method?
options: a:Accelerate and steer back on the road quickly.,b:Immediately pull all the way off of the road and get back on when it is safe.,c:Take your foot off the accelerator, steer parallel to the road, then ease back onto the pavement.
note: If your right wheels leave the pavement, ease off the gas, steer parallel to the road, slow, and carefully ease back onto the roadway when safe.

question: In fog, rain, or snow, which headlights should be used?
options: a:Low beams.,b:High beams.,c:Fog lights only.
note: Low beams are used in fog, rain, or snow because high beams reflect off precipitation and reduce visibility.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, glance:
options: a:Over your left shoulder.,b:At your side mirror.,c:Over your right shoulder.
note: Check the blind spot by turning your head and looking over the shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter.

question: What is the key rule about speed control in curves?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve.,b:Speed up slightly before the curve then brake at the sharpest point.,c:Maintain the same speed at all times.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve so inertia won't carry you outward and you can maintain control.

question: Being distracted while driving usually causes which effect on the driver?
options: a:Usually causes the driver to drive faster.,b:Usually causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.,c:Is never dangerous.
note: Distractions delay a driver's reactions to traffic and hazards and are never safe.

question: At a light rail intersection, what should you always do?
options: a:Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.,b:Look both ways before crossing tracks and obey signals.,c:Drive around lowered crossing gates when safe.
note: Never drive around lowered gates; always look both ways before crossing tracks and obey signs and traffic signals.

question: Which actions can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allow extra travel time, obey speed limits, and use proper signals.,b:Speed up to pass aggressive drivers.,c:Ignore turn signals from others.
note: Being patient, following speed limits, and signaling properly help reduce aggressive encounters on the road.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road.,b:Switch to high beams.,c:Turn your lights on and off.
note: Avoid looking directly at the oncoming lights; glance toward the right edge of your lane until the other vehicle passes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When moving from the left lane into the right lane, you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles before changing lanes.,b:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder before changing lanes.,c:Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders before changing lanes.
note: Check mirrors and blind spots by glancing over the shoulder in the direction you want to move, and signal before changing lanes.

question: What do illuminated brake lights tell drivers behind you?
options: a:You are slowing down or stopping.,b:You are making a turn.,c:Your emergency brake is on.,d:You are reversing.
note: Brake lights signal to following drivers that you are decelerating or stopping; keep them in working order for safety.

question: What is a 'No zone'?
options: a:The blind spot of a large vehicle,b:A designated no passing zone,c:A one-way traffic area
note: 'No zones' are the large blind spots around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles disappear from the driver's view.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To safely pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Move into the lane used by oncoming traffic to complete the pass when safe and legal.,b:Use the shoulder to pass.,c:Never cross the centerline to pass.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road requires using the oncoming traffic lane; only pass when it is safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever permitted to drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle?
options: a:No, never.,b:Only if the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:Only on two-or-more-lane roads.,d:If traffic ahead is stopped.
note: Do not pass by driving off the pavement onto the shoulder; passing must be done within the traveled lanes when legal and safe.

question: How can you stay aware of traffic behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Constantly turn and look out your back window.,c:Leave large gaps in front of you only.,d:Block other vehicles' views.
note: Regularly check rearview and side mirrors to monitor traffic behind and adjust driving as necessary.

question: When you hear or see an emergency vehicle on a divided multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, move to provide a clear path, and stop.,b:Disregard it if there are other lanes available.,c:Stop as quickly as possible in your lane.,d:Speed up to create distance.
note: On a multilane highway yield by moving over and stopping when safe to allow an emergency vehicle a clear path.

question: Following a large truck on the freeway, you should:
options: a:Follow farther behind than you would a passenger vehicle.,b:Follow no more than one car length behind the truck.,c:Follow closely because the driver can see farther ahead than you can.
note: Leave extra space when following large trucks so you can see around them and give yourself time to react.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood, what effect does it have?
options: a:It slows your reactions and makes you feel more confident.,b:It makes your reactions faster.,c:It metabolizes more quickly on its own.
note: Alcohol slows reaction time, impairs coordination and judgment, and often increases risky confidence, raising crash risk.

question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding left, you should:
options: a:Turn the steering wheel left (toward the skid) to help regain control.,b:Turn the wheel right to correct the skid.,c:Not move the steering wheel.
note: If the rear slides left, steer in the direction of the skid to regain control; do not panic or slam on brakes.

question: What is the only medically proven way to remove alcohol from your system?
options: a:Give your body time.,b:Drink coffee.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and remove alcohol; remedies like coffee, showers, or exercise do not lower BAC.

question: Which roadway is most likely to be slippery after snow or rain in cold weather?
options: a:A road in a shaded area.,b:A residential road.,c:A hilly, open road.
note: Shaded portions of the roadway can freeze and remain icy longer than sun-exposed areas.

question: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always indicates what?
options: a:Hospital sign.,b:Speed limit sign.,c:Stop sign.
note: An eight-sided sign is always a stop sign; come to a complete stop when you encounter it.

question: What ability does alcohol affect first?
options: a:Judgment.,b:Vision.,c:Balance.
note: Alcohol first impairs judgment and decision-making, which then leads to deteriorations in other driving skills.

question: Which following distance is recommended for an inexperienced driver under normal conditions?
options: a:At least three seconds.,b:Two seconds is sufficient.,c:One second if traffic is light.,d:Four to five seconds at all speeds.
note: Inexperienced drivers should maintain at least a three-second following distance in normal conditions; increase it in poor conditions or at higher speeds.

question: Which is a safe driving technique?
options: a:Using high beam headlights in fog.,b:Staring fixedly at the road ahead.,c:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently and scanning the road.,d:Driving with only parking lights at night.
note: Scan the road and check rearview mirrors every 2–5 seconds; do not stare fixedly ahead and avoid high beams in fog.

question: A flashing red traffic light means:
options: a:Proceed with caution without stopping.,b:The same as a stop sign—you must stop.,c:The signal is malfunctioning and can be ignored.,d:Yield but do not stop.
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop; yield to traffic and pedestrians and proceed only when safe.

question: Should you use low beam headlights while driving in fog?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Low beams or fog lights should be used in fog to reduce backscatter and improve visibility.

question: What should you do when roads are slippery from rain, snow, or ice?
options: a:Slow down and drive more cautiously than the posted speed.,b:Drive the posted speed limit without change.,c:Speed up to pass unsafe drivers.,d:Use cruise control to maintain steady speed.
note: Reduce speed and make changes in speed and direction more gradually to maintain control on slippery surfaces.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low-beam headlights.,c:High-beam headlights.
note: Use low-beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect and reduce visibility further.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On an interstate, how can you best avoid conflicts with traffic merging from on-ramps to your right?
options: a:Change lanes to the left when traffic permits.,b:Slow down so merging vehicles can go ahead.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: When safe and traffic permits, move out of the right lane to allow merging traffic from on-ramps.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Take a break.,b:Try to fight it by rolling down the windows.,c:Take caffeine pills and continue driving.
note: If you feel drowsy, stop at the next safe place to rest, nap, or switch drivers; short-term stimulants are not a substitute for rest.

question: At dawn, dusk, or during rain or snow when visibility is reduced, you should turn on:
options: a:Your headlights (low beams).,b:Your parking lights.,c:Instrument panel lights only.
note: Use low-beam headlights when visibility is reduced or when windshield wipers are required to improve others seeing you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Motorcycles are entitled to:
options: a:The bicycle lane only.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:Half the width of a lane.,d:Parking on sidewalks.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full lane width just like other vehicles and should be given adequate space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection at the posted speed and the light turns yellow, you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection if it is safe to do so.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Proceed through without caution.
note: A steady yellow light warns the signal will turn red; stop if you can do so safely, otherwise proceed with caution.

question: Approximately how much alcohol does the average person's body eliminate per hour?
options: a:About one standard alcoholic drink per hour.,b:About three drinks per hour.,c:None—alcohol remains indefinitely.,d:Two drinks per hour.
note: On average the body metabolizes about one standard drink per hour, though this varies by individual factors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who goes first?
options: a:The driver who arrives first.,b:The driver who arrives last.,c:The driver on the left.,d:The largest vehicle.
note: At four-way stops the first vehicle to arrive goes first. If two arrive simultaneously, the driver on the left yields to the driver on the right.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Look over your left or right shoulder to view the blind spot.,b:Rely only on your side mirrors.,c:Look only at the rearview mirror.,d:Use your horn before moving.
note: Mirrors do not show all areas; always glance over the shoulder toward the direction of the lane change to check blind spots.

question: At a red light that includes a green arrow for your lane, you may proceed in the arrow's direction when:
options: a:You are in the proper lane and the way is clear.,b:You have first come to a complete stop.,c:You wait for the main light to turn green.
note: If your lane shows a green arrow, you may proceed in that direction when the roadway is clear, even if the main signal is red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are out due to power failure, how should drivers proceed?
options: a:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and proceed when it is your turn.,b:Turn on hazard lights and drive through without stopping.,c:Use hand signals to direct traffic yourself.,d:Wait until power is restored before crossing.
note: When signals are out, yield and proceed as at a four-way stop: stop, then go in order of arrival while watching for others.

question: What is the standard top-to-bottom order of traffic signal lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Green, yellow, red.,c:Red, green, yellow.,d:Yellow, red, green.
note: The standard vertical order for traffic signals is red at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom.

question: To whom must you give the right-of-way when they are crossing a street?
options: a:Any pedestrian in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.,b:Only pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,c:Pedestrians wearing reflective clothing only.,d:No pedestrians have automatic priority.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks and should exercise caution at all crossings.

question: When driving in fog, you should use which headlights?
options: a:Use your low beam headlights.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your high beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights (or fog lights if equipped) in fog; high beams reflect off the fog and reduce visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming traffic going straight.,b:No one when turning left.,c:Only pedestrians.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming vehicles and wait until they can complete the turn safely.

question: A broken yellow centerline between two lanes of traffic means:
options: a:Passing is permitted when it's safe.,b:Both lanes of traffic are going the same direction.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A dashed or broken yellow line separates opposing traffic and indicates passing is legal when safe and clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a right turn, your vehicle should be positioned:
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:As far to the right side of the road as practicable.,d:At the left edge of the lane.
note: Get as far to the right as possible before a right turn; do not cut across lanes to make the turn.

question: How should you safely pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Slow down and give them as much space as possible.,b:Drive in the bicycle lane until you get a chance to pass.,c:Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you're trying to pass.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and leave plenty of lateral space; do not crowd or startle the cyclist.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and slash through it indicates:
options: a:An action is forbidden.,b:Drivers should come to a complete stop.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.
note: A red circle with a diagonal slash over a symbol means the action shown is prohibited by law.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?
options: a:Follow the crossing guard’s directions.,b:Ignore the crossing guard and follow surrounding traffic.,c:Assume the crossing guard is not authorized.,d:Drive faster to clear the area quickly.
note: Crossing guards are authorized to direct traffic in school zones; obey their instructions and exercise extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer orders you to stop even though the traffic signal is green, what should you do?
options: a:Obey the officer.,b:Obey the traffic signal instead.,c:Follow the vehicle in front of you.
note: Drivers must obey directions from a police officer even if they contradict traffic signals or signs.

question: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend up to how far behind them?
options: a:TRUE,b:FALSE
note: Large vehicles have blind spots that can extend far behind them (up to about 200 feet); do not tailgate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an intersection from different highways at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left,b:The vehicle on the right,c:Either one
note: When two vehicles arrive simultaneously at an intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

question: Which statement about alcohol and driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol affects judgement needed to drive safely.,b:If you can walk in a straight line, it is safe to drive.,c:If under the legal BAC limit, your driving is unaffected.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, reaction time, and coordination; even amounts below the legal limit can adversely affect driving ability.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights you should:
options: a:Stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted before proceeding.,b:Drive around the gates if you don't see a train.,c:Slow and drive around the gates.
note: Never cross when gates are down or lights are flashing; wait until all warning devices are silent and gates are raised.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the pass.,b:Speed up to prevent the pass.,c:Maintain the same speed and position.,d:Brake suddenly to discourage the pass.
note: Reduce speed slightly to give the passing driver space to complete the maneuver safely and quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which must you obey over the others: a steady red light, a police officer, or a stop sign?
options: a:A steady red light,b:A police officer,c:A stop sign,d:None of the above
note: Directions from traffic officers take precedence over signs, signals, and pavement markings.

question: If stopped by a police officer, what should you do while waiting for the officer?
options: a:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window immediately.,b:Get your paperwork out before the officer reaches the car and exit.,c:Stay in the vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.,d:Step out of the vehicle and approach the officer.
note: Remain in your vehicle with hands visible, and wait until the officer asks for your license, registration, and insurance.

question: Which devices are used on some highways to guide drivers into proper turn lanes?
options: a:Lane-use arrows and markings.,b:Flashing red lights.,c:White lines on the side of the road.,d:Temporary cones only.
note: Arrows painted on the pavement and lane markings direct drivers into specific lanes for turning or continuing straight.

question: To prepare for anything upcoming on the road ahead, you should:
options: a:Continuously scan the entire road and roadsides.,b:Stare straight ahead at all times.,c:Drive with your left foot on the brake.
note: Constantly scan far ahead and to the sides to spot hazards early and give yourself time to react.

question: Work zone signs indicate:
options: a:It is summer.,b:That you must immediately stop and back up.,c:That less-than-ideal driving conditions are present—use caution.,d:Detour routes only.
note: Orange work zone signs warn that road work is present; drive carefully and obey reduced speed limits.

question: 'Highway hypnosis' can result from:
options: a:Staring at the roadway for extended periods without scanning.,b:Taking frequent rest breaks.,c:Getting too much sleep before driving.,d:Listening to music at low volume.
note: Highway hypnosis occurs when you stare ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning, increasing crash risk due to zoning out.

question: A flashing yellow light as you approach an intersection means:
options: a:Stop before crossing.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Wait for a green light.,d:Yield to all traffic then proceed without caution.
note: A flashing yellow light indicates you should slow down, check for cross traffic, and proceed carefully.

question: When you approach a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait until the stop arm is withdrawn.,b:Honk before passing on the left.,c:Proceed if you think the children are finished crossing.
note: Whenever a school bus displays its stop signal, drivers must stop and not proceed until the stop arm is retracted and the roadway is clear.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you should:
options: a:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.,b:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,c:Slightly increase your speed.
note: Construction zones often have workers, slow equipment, and lane shifts; reduce speed and be prepared to stop or change lanes safely.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street, what must you do?
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Drive to the right edge and slow down.,c:Stay in your lane and let it pass without stopping.
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using lights/sirens by pulling to the right edge and stopping until they pass.

question: Why exercise caution when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bicycle.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:You are moving faster than the bicycle.
note: When you pull out to pass a cyclist, oncoming vehicles might not see you; ensure enough space and time before passing.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is traveling in your area, what should you do?
options: a:Make every effort to give it a clear path of travel.,b:Stop immediately in your lane and prevent passage.,c:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: Pull to the side or otherwise clear the path when safe to allow emergency vehicles to pass quickly and safely.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a railroad crossing gate while it is being lowered or raised?
options: a:Yes, if you first look carefully in both directions.,b:Yes, if your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,c:No, never drive around or under a lowering/raising gate.
note: Flashing lights, bells, and lowered gates mean stop; never drive around or under a gate that is moving. Only cross when gates are fully raised and signals have stopped.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction from water on the road (hydroplaning), how should you respond?
options: a:Apply the brakes firmly to stop the skid.,b:Maintain a constant speed to regain traction.,c:Slow down gradually and avoid using the brakes until you regain traction.
note: When hydroplaning, ease off the accelerator and slow gradually without braking; braking can worsen the skid.

question: As your speed increases, you should:
options: a:Look well ahead of your vehicle to allow time to react.,b:Pass more frequently to keep up with traffic.,c:Turn on headlights earlier.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance; scanning far ahead gives more time to respond to hazards.

question: To drive safely at night, you should do which of the following?
options: a:Increase following distance and ensure headlights are working properly.,b:Only drive if you are young and alert.,c:Use parking lights instead of headlights.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance, avoid driving when tired, and ensure your headlights are properly adjusted and working.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you tell it's safe to return to your lane after passing another car?
options: a:If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.,c:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
note: Before returning after a pass, ensure there's a safe gap; it's safe when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: When does stopping distance increase?
options: a:On a wet or icy road.,b:On paved highways.,c:When driving at night.
note: Stopping distances increase on wet, icy, or loose surfaces (gravel, stones) because traction is reduced.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you always signal?
options: a:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.,b:When changing lanes.,c:Pulling into or out of a parking space.
note: Use turn signals for any movement to the left or right: changing lanes, pulling into traffic, and pulling in/out of parking spaces.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Checking antifreeze and windshield washer fluid is especially important in winter.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
note: Do not use cruise control on snow, ice, rain, or similar hazardous conditions. Winter driving requires extra caution and vehicle maintenance checks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle going the same direction, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:About three seconds after passing.,c:When you can no longer see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: Only return to your lane when you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and the lane is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the lane closest to the one you were in (the nearest lane).,b:Into the far right lane.,c:Into any lane you want.,d:Into the middle lane only.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, turn into the lane nearest to the lane you came from unless road markings indicate otherwise.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is correct?
options: a:Always ensure every passenger uses a seat belt or proper child restraint.,b:Airbags alone provide sufficient protection for infants.,c:Infants should always sit in the front seat.,d:Seat belts are optional for short trips.
note: Seat belts and approved child restraints greatly reduce injury risk; children 12 and under should ride properly restrained in the rear seat.

question: Drinking coffee after consuming alcohol will:
options: a:Has no effect on blood alcohol concentration.,b:Cancels the effect of the alcohol.,c:Decreases blood alcohol concentration.
note: Coffee or other stimulants do not reduce your BAC or sober you up; only time removes alcohol from your system.

question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights flashing, you must pull over:
options: a:To the right edge of the road and stop, regardless of direction of approach.,b:Only if it is behind you.,c:Only if it is coming from the opposite direction.
note: You must pull to the right edge and stop for emergency vehicles using lights and/or sirens, whether approaching from front or rear.

question: When in line to cross a railroad track with no gates or signals, what must you ensure?
options: a:That there is space beyond the tracks for your vehicle to get completely across.,b:That you may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,c:That you have right-of-way and need not check for trains.,d:That your vehicle can stop on the tracks if needed.
note: Never enter tracks unless you can clear them fully; do not pass other vehicles as you approach or cross railroad tracks.
